item.title: Tinubu Congratulates Flamingos, Backs Team To Win U-17 World Cup
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their 3-1 victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. In a statement issued by his media aide, Bayo Onanuga, the President described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad. Tinubu also commended the coaching crew and everyone whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign. As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, the President urged the players to remain focused, confident and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill and unwavering support of Nigerians. “I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title. “I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited. “Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. President Bola Tinubu The Flamingos reached the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time after defeating Brazil 3-1 in their semi-final encounter in Morocco. The Nigerian girls produced a spirited second-half performance, scoring three goals before Brazil grabbed a late consolation. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute, finishing off an assist from Oluwakemi Adegubyi to give Nigeria the lead. The Flamingos doubled their advantage in the 71st minute when Awawu Bashiru found the net, with Joseph providing the assist. Bashiru struck again in the 80th minute to make it 3-0, converting a pass from Oluebube Umejiaku as Nigeria took firm control of the encounter. Brazil pulled one back in the 89th minute through Greise Kelly, assisted by Yasmin Queiroz, but the goal came too late to prevent Nigeria from securing victory and a place in the final. The post Tinubu Congratulates Flamingos, Backs Team To Win U-17 World Cup appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Yamal Makes History As Barça Ends Villa’s UCL Run
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Jerome Miron Barcelona crushed Aston Villa 3-0 on Tuesday night in Spain, ending the English side’s perfect start to the UEFA Champions League. The rain poured down at Camp Nou, but that did not stop the home team from dominating the match. An error by João Gomes in the seventh minute allowed Lamine Yamal to score first. Yamal now holds the record as the competition’s top-scoring teenager with 14 total goals. He now holds the record that once belonged to Kylian Mbappé. Raphinha took over the game in the second half, scoring two more goals to seal the win. In only 13 appearances, he has accumulated 19 goals for this season. The victory puts Barcelona and Villa both at nine points in the standings, though Villa’s perfect record is now gone. This result shows the power of the young Spanish talent against a strong Premier League opponent. According to ESPN , the win helps Hansi Flick’s team regain momentum after losing two big games last month. A Historic Night for Youth The biggest story of the night belongs to the young winger who changed the history books. Yamal did not just score a goal; he broke a record that stood for years. He scored his 14th goal in the competition, surpassing the mark set by the French superstar Kylian Mbappé. This achievement highlights how quickly the new generation is taking over the sport. The Brazilian midfielder João Gomes made a costly mistake that led directly to the first goal. Yamal capitalized on that error with a trademark finish around the goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. Barcelona’s press forced the error that gave them the lead. The rain made the field slick, but the young player found a way to score. He cut inside on his left foot and placed the ball perfectly past the helpless keeper. This moment proved that experience does not always beat raw talent and speed. The crowd at Camp Nou saw a future legend rise on a Tuesday night in November. Raphinha Leads the Attack Raphinha stepped up when the game mattered most in the second half. He has been playing as a striker under coach Hansi Flick since 2024, and his numbers show his value. His goal in the 52nd minute had a bit of luck, as the shot deflected past the keeper. The second goal, however, was a pure poacher’s finish following brilliant work from João Cancelo. According to ESPN, Raphinha has now scored 32 goals alongside Yamal out of Barcelona’s 60 total goals this season. These two players are the engine of the team. They have netted 32 of the team’s 60 goals in just 15 matches. Raphinha secured his seventh Champions League double, maintaining his lead as Europe’s top scorer across the top five leagues this season. His ability to play as a No. 9 has reached a new dimension this year. The Brazilian winger is proving he can carry the offensive load for the entire club. item.title: Knicks' Mike Brown makes stance on ex-Laker Dalton Knecht crystal clear after debut vs. Bulls
item.description: Knicks' Mike Brown makes stance on ex-Laker Dalton Knecht crystal clear after debut vs. Bulls originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This season has already been a rollercoaster for former Los Angeles Lakers first-round pick Dalton Knecht, and it hasn’t been long at all. Knecht was once considered the steal of the 2024 NBA Draft by Los Angeles. However, things have not gone according to plan after he saw limited playing time last season. The Lakers eventually ran out of plans for him, which is why they waived him before the season began to make room on the roster. “The Los Angeles Lakers are waiving 2024 No. 17 pick Dalton Knecht, sources tell ESPN,” ESPN’s Shams Charania wrote. Knecht became a highly sought-after free agent once he cleared waivers. After being one of the Lakers' best-kept secrets early in his career, he could become one of the team's biggest mistakes as time goes on. The former first-round pick ultimately decided to sign with the New York Knicks . “Former Lakers forward Dalton Knecht has agreed to sign with the New York Knicks on a two-way NBA contract, his agents at Excel Sports Management tell ESPN," Charania wrote. On Wednesday night, Knecht made his Knicks debut against the Chicago Bulls . The former Laker had a productive night off the bench, finishing with 10 points and seven rebounds. After the game, New York head coach Mike Brown made it clear that he views Knecht as a scorer, not just a shooter. “He's a scorer. He's not just a shooter. A lot of people think he's a shooter because he's white. I said it for you. I hope I don't get in trouble,” Brown told the media. There is no doubt that Brown made his thoughts on Knecht clear. Defensively, Knecht may still struggle at times, but he looked closer to his former self on offense. It was a great night for the Knicks all around, and Knecht took advantage of the opportunity in front of him. Brown clearly thinks highly of him as a scorer, so it will be interesting to see how Knecht's role evolves moving forward. item.title: Kane's Kompany pact! Striker salutes boss and opens up on bold decision to ditch Spurs comfort zone
item.description: Manchester City v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Harry Kane opened up on his strong working relationship with Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany following his contract extension until 2029. The striker also reflected on his choice to swap Premier League familiarity at Tottenham for a challenge in Germany. Perfect alignment between star striker and manager Harry Kane’s decision to commit his long-term future to FC Bayern reflects a strong tactical and mental alignment with manager Vincent Kompany. Since Kompany took charge, Kane has maintained his elite scoring rate while serving as a key leader in the dressing room. The striker revealed that Kompany allowed him total space and freedom when deciding his future. "He might have only found out this morning, I've not had any contact with him in the last few days! He never put pressure on me," Kane said. Respect for Kompany's relentless driving mentality Kane detailed how Kompany's coaching philosophy matches his own professional standards, regardless of a player's stature or experience. "We had an open chat about four weeks ago, but that was more general... I respect the coach a lot, the way he drives everyone," Kane explained. "Regardless of whether they've got 500 games under their belt or is new to the game. That's also my mentality, so we suit each other well." "I imagined challenging for the league, the cup and the Champions League every year... I've always believed in myself. Wherever I've played, I've scored goals," he added. Leaving Premier League comfort zone proved correct Reflecting on his departure from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023, Kane expressed zero regrets about leaving the English top flight to test himself abroad. "I spent a lot of time in the Premier League, I always watched them a lot. It's nice to have a change of scenery," Kane noted. "And sometimes a change is also good mentally... When I'm older, I'll look back and say this was the right step, to get out of my comfort zone." "The belief in yourself is an important factor. I feel as good as ever here. We'll be playing at the highest level in the next few years," the England captain affirmed. Kompany and Kane forge forward together With both manager and star forward aligned, Bayern look positioned to maintain a steady tactical foundation over the coming seasons. Kompany will rely on Kane's work ethic to drive the team's pressing structure and attacking fluidity. The pair now turn their full attention back to defending their domestic titles and challenging for European honors.

item.title: The Sabres’ Dylan Larkin Problem Isn’t the Assets
item.description: Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin has been suspended without pay since Oct. 29 , when he told the team he no longer wanted to be part of the organization, and a Dylan Larkin trade is still stuck behind the market he has limited himself to. He has given the Red Wings a list of 10 teams he would accept a deal to, and the Buffalo Sabres are not one of them. Why a Dylan Larkin trade to Buffalo is complicated Matthew Fairburn of The Athletic , who covers the Sabres, took a fan mailbag question Wednesday about whether Buffalo could get into the Larkin market at all. “But the Sabres are not on his expanded 10-team trade list. How much will that list have to expand before Buffalo ends up on it? Are the Sabres even a more attractive option than simply staying in Detroit? Yes, Buffalo ended its playoff drought, but that’s still just one year. Assuming he doesn’t want to go to a Canadian team, that leaves 26 teams. “I wonder if the Sabres would get on the list if it got to 15 teams? Would it take 20? And how much more would the Sabres have to pay for the Red Wings to be compelled to move him within the division? All of those questions make me hesitant to get people too excited about the idea. I also think the Sabres should be wary about adding a player who essentially needs to be begged to come to Buffalo. You don’t want to be someone’s 15th choice when you’re giving up the assets required to get a player like Larkin.” Oct 31, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Kings defenseman Drew Doughty (8) lands on the ice as he battles Buffalo Sabres defenseman Louis Crevier (46) and left wing Zach Benson (6) for the puck during the third period at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Larkin’s camp has already said no to a longer list Fairburn’s question about how far the list would have to stretch already has an answer, and it is not an encouraging one for Buffalo. Larkin started with three teams and expanded to 10: the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. TSN hockey insider Pierre LeBrun reported Tuesday that Buffalo is one of the teams sitting off that list, along with Montreal, Boston and Los Angeles, and that Larkin’s camp, led by agent Pat Brisson, has told the Red Wings no again in recent days. That is the part of this that matters most to Sabres fans. Buffalo does not need Larkin to warm to the idea of Buffalo in general. It needs him to add the one team in his own division that would cost Detroit the most to do business with. Larkin is in the fourth season of an eight-year contract with an annual cap hit of $8.7 million, and he is forfeiting roughly $41,000 a day while the suspension runs. item.title: 2027: Makinde rejects ‘turn-by-turn’ presidency, vows APM victory
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has vowed to win the 2027 election, urging Nigerians to reject what he described as ‘turn-by-turn nepotism’ in choosing the country’s president. Makinde spoke at the party’s South-West town hall meeting, where he argued that the region should not be expected to support President Bola Tinubu solely because he hails from the area. Citing the 1999 presidential election, he said the South-West had presented Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae as competing candidates, allowing Nigerians to choose their preferred leader. “As a matter of fact, what the South-West did was to present two of its finest candidates, two of its best, for Nigerians to choose from. Is there anything wrong with doing that this time around?” he asked. Makinde warned that treating the presidency as a regional entitlement could encourage sectional policies at the expense of national development. “We do not want turn-by-turn nepotism. We also do not want a situation where someone says, ‘I will execute projects in my zone because it is my turn,’” he said. The Oyo governor also accused the Federal Government of frustrating opposition parties, warning that democracy could not thrive under a political system that stifled competition. “There is no democracy in a one-party system,” he declared. On the economy, Makinde advocated a shift from dependence on federal allocations to productive economic activities that would create wealth and expand government revenue. “When they are productive, they become prosperous. When they become prosperous, tax their prosperity. Do not tax poverty,” he said. APM National Leader and Bauchi State Governor, Senator Bala Mohammed, described Makinde as a tested politician whose record in Oyo State informed the party’s decision to present him as its presidential candidate. “He understands Nigeria’s problems, particularly in infrastructure and public services. He has demonstrated his capacity to deliver by reducing infrastructure gaps at the sub-national level,” Mohammed said. The party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, described the South-West meeting as encouraging, claiming the turnout indicated growing support for Makinde. National Chairman Yusuf Dantalle criticised insecurity, rising petroleum prices and what he described as the erosion of electoral accountability. “We must reset Nigeria. This is not democracy. It is no longer the votes of the people that determine who wins,” Dantalle said. The post 2027: Makinde rejects ‘turn-by-turn’ presidency, vows APM victory appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jaguars’ Week 9 injury report vs. Ravens: Bhayshul Tuten designation makes for tricky fantasy decision
item.description: Travis Register-Imagn Images Jaguars’ Week 9 injury report vs. Ravens: Bhayshul Tuten designation makes for tricky fantasy decision appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars will be facing the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football, as they look to continue to add to their win total. They’ve played well on both sides of the ball this season, but it’s been the offense that has been able to have a lot of success, and Trevor Lawrence is getting everyone involved. As for the Ravens, they haven’t been able to have much consistency because of injuries, specifically to their quarterbacks. After returning from injury last week, Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury on the first play of the game and was ruled out. Tyler Huntley then came in, and he suffered turf toe, which will cause him to miss the rest of the season. That means that Joe Fagnano will start against the Jaguars. The Jaguars have a few injuries coming into this game, with Bhayshul Tuten being one of them. He’s been dealing with a foot and ankle injury and hasn’t practiced all week because of it. Nonetheless, he’s still listed as questionable for the game, but it’s hard to see him suiting up if he hasn’t practiced. Tuten is supposed to be a game-time decision , so his status is truly up in the air right now. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) If fantasy football owners have another option to use at the running back position, it may be best for you to use them instead of banking on Tuten to play. Even if he does play, it’s uncertain how much of an impact he’d make on the field, and he might end up splitting most of his snaps with Chris Rodriguez Jr. Tuten did have a big game against the Indianapolis Colts, where he finished with 104 yards and a touchdown. When he’s fully healthy, he’s a must-start. With him being a game-time decision, it’s hard to know what you’ll truly get from him. item.title: Brittney Griner lands unique role ahead of Unrivaled’s third season
item.description: Brittney Griner lands unique role ahead of Unrivaled’s third season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Brittney Griner's legendary WNBA career is winding down. Sure, Griner is still capable of dropping 25 points on any given night, and she's still capable of dominating defensively as the WNBA's active leader in blocks per game. But the fact is, Griner turned 36 last month, and the forthcoming 2027 season -- where she will return home to Texas as a member of the rebooted Houston Comets -- is almost certain to be her last in The W. MORE : Olivia Miles brings buzz to Unrivaled amid Hive roster reveal Griner's role in Unrivaled for the upcoming season serves as some confirmation that the nine-time All-Star is actively preparing for the next phase of her career in basketball. Griner has been named as one of six players in Unrivaled's six-player development pool for the 2027 season, which begins Jan. 8 with four games in Boston and Inglewood, Calif. The Player Pool has entered the chat. 👀 https://t.co/GwQkEbJapa — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 4, 2026 But critically, Griner will have a special role within the Player Pool. Unrivaled has named Griner as the head of the 3-on-3 league's new Player Coach Development Program, where the two-time WNBA Defensive Player of the Year "will develop her leadership and coaching skills while continuing to compete on the court." Griner will receive mentorship in this department from Unrivaled's head coaches, as well as "hands-on" coaching experience. The wheels were put in motion for Griner's transition into coaching during the 2026 season in Connecticut, where Griner sat in on film sessions in a sort of "coaching internship" role. That role will be expanded in Unrivaled, as Griner continues laying the groundwork for her post-playing career. item.title: Who is Molly Miller? Get to know viral Arizona State basketball coach
item.description: Into today’s day and age, nothing can throw you into the spotlight like viral fame, and that has been the case over the past three years for Molly Miller , who is entering her second year as head coach of the Arizona State women’s basketball team. Miller recently went viral for an incredible rallying cry for her team ahead of Year 2 , and again went viral a few days later for her sideline fit . Before joining Arizona State, Miller was one of the brightest young stars in college basketball , leading the Grand Canyon women’s basketball team to a NCAA Tournament appearance. The WAC Coach of the Year led the Antelopes to an impressive 32-3 record, going a perfect 16-0 in conference play and winning the Western Athletic Conference regular season title and conference tournament. Now, she’s back in the spotlight and fans can’t get enough of seeing what Miller can continue to do leading the Sun Devils, after going 24-11 with an NCAA Tournament berth in her first season. MORE: ASU cheerleaders greet Molly Miller, new Sun Devils women’s basketball coach Get To Know Molly Miller Oct 20, 2026; Kansas City, MO, USA; Arizona State coach Molly Miller interviews during the Big 12 Media Days event at T-Mobile Center. Mandatory Credit: William Purnell-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Before joining the coaching ranks, Miller was a star point guard at Drury University, scoring 1,570 career points and earning a spot in the Great Lakes Valley Conference Hall of Fame. From there, she turned to coaching, where she was immediately finding success leading her alma mater. MORE: Arizona State women’s basketball coach Molly Miller rewarded after breakout season As head coach at Drury University, Miller compiled an impressive 180-17 record, with four Great Lakes Valley Conference titles and a Final Four appearance in the 2019 NCAA Division II Tournament. Drury head coach Molly Miller cuts down the net after winning the NCAA Division II Midwest Regional Championship game 51-44 over Grand Valley at the O’Reilly Family Event Center on Monday, March 18, 2019. Drury3 Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) That led Miller to Grand Canyon University for the next five years, where she was once again an overwhelming success. At GCU, the Lopes went 117-38 during Miller’s tenure, including a 30-game winning streak, WAC title, and the first-ever NCAA Tournament berth in school history. That’s when she finally got a shot in the big show. GCU head coach Molly Miller high-fives her team after a win against ASU during a game at Footprint Center on Nov. 14, 2024, in Phoenix, Ariz. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) After her inaugural season leading the Sun Devils, Miller was immediately rewarded with a new contract extension. The multi-year deal will keep Miller at Arizona State through April 30, 2031. item.title: Five Reasons Nebraska Will Win: Illinois
item.description: Well, it’s November. The Huskers are 5-3 and just need one more win to once again become bowl eligible. Some of you may have counted them out after the soul crushing path these last few games have led us down, but I haven’t! This week is about redemption. This week the Huskers are going to come out on fire and cruise their way to win number six. These are your reasons why: #1 THE DEFENSE The Husker defense has been the backbone of this team. They are the reason that the Huskers were still in the game and ahead in the fourth quarter in each of the last three games. This defense will be sharp against a balanced Illinois attack and will be ready to cause some takeaways. #2 RUNNING ROOM Nebraska has not seen a lot of offense in the last three games. They’ve been low scoring and aside from a couple drives the Huskers have found it hard to move the ball. That changes this week. The offensive line is going to get a good push on the Illini defense and will give the running backs plenty of running room. Also, for the Huskers to win, we are going to need to see more of Jamal Rule on the field. Isaiah Mozee and Mekhi Nelson do fine, but the rushing game was so much stronger with Rule leading the pack. #3 Anthony Colandrea Anthony Colandrea has been leading this team. He has done all he can to get this team to win. Last week was a rough one for him, he threw three interceptions. I think it’s hard to always blame the quarterback for those, when part of the problem is receivers not running the routes that they need to be. Regardless of last week, Colandrea will be back on that field and he will be ready to lead this Husker team to a victory. He will be ready and we will be cheering for him as he dashes down field for a Husker touchdown. #4 THE RULE OF THREES Good and bad things come in threes. Illinois is on a three game winning streak, Nebraska is on a three game losing streak. Now that they have both accomplished those tasks in threes, they must switch and go the other direction. Therefore, Nebraska will win and Illinois will lose. It’s basic science and math really. #5 IT’S FRIDAY NIGHT Nebraska and Illinois are playing on a Friday night for their third consecutive meeting. The Huskers won the first game in 2023 20-7, Illinois won the second game 31-24 in overtime. It is only logical then that the Huskers will win the third one. You know, because they are trading every other win. It’s something a polite team would do and I know Illinois is nothing if they aren’t polite. I can’t wait to talk to you all next week when the Huskers are bowl eligible and looking for win #7. CLICK BELOW TO VOTE IN THIS WEEK’S CORN NATION REACTS SURVEY!

item.title: Confirmed: Seven Barcelona academy players named in Spain U17 World Cup squad
item.description: Confirmed: Seven Barcelona academy players named in Spain U17 World Cup squad As many as seven Barcelona youth talents will be a part of the Spain national team squad at the upcoming U17 FIFA World Cup in Qatar. Indeed, manager David Cubillo has called up seven exciting La Masia talents in the form of Raul Exposito, Sergi Mayans, Baba Kourouma, Jordi Pesquer, Ebrima Tunkara, Roberto Tomas and Iu Martinez. Of the seven players, four happen to be defenders: Exposito, Mayans, Kourouma, and Pesquer, who has already had some experience in the first-team dynamics, having participated in the pre-season during the summer. Meanwhile, Tunkara, who continues to be called up to first-team training regularly, and Roberto Tomas will be the midfielders representing Barça at the U17 World Cup with Spain. Iu Martinez is the only forward from La Masia to be called up for the tournament. The seven Barça players will report for the training camp in Madrid on 9 November before flying to Qatar for the tournament. As such, they will miss an important stretch of matches with the club’s youth and reserve teams. Spain have been drawn in Group H, along with Morocco, Fiji, and China. Having never won the U17 World Cup, they will be eager to follow in the footsteps of the senior national team and the U15 side and lift the trophy.

item.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Tight End Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Kyle Pitts vs. Brenton Strange
item.description: Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. (8) catches a five-yard touchdown pass against the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Not every fantasy football manager is lucky enough to start one of the elite TEs each week. Among the other fantasy-viable TEs, Kyle Pitts and Brenton Strange are ranked similarly in Week 9. Between Pitts and Strange, which TE is the better play in fantasy football in Week 9? All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros . Kyle Pitts Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. (8) celebrates after a touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Pitts was limited to only 2.6 fantasy points in Week 8, but that was against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a far-from-ideal weather game. From Week 5 to Week 7, Pitts was the TE4 in fantasy points per game (17.1). Among 28 TEs with 25-plus targets, Pitts has the fifth-most touchdowns (4) and the eighth-most yards after the catch per reception (6.1). In Week 9, Pitts will face a Cincinnati Bengals defense that is permitting the fourth-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to TEs (+5.3). Brenton Strange Jacksonville Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange (85) catches a pass during the first quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a slow start to the season, Strange is the TE12 in fantasy points per game (11.8) since Week 4. Strange gets solid volume in an efficient Jacksonville Jaguars offense, generating the 14th-highest target share (18.0%) at the TE position. Entering Week 9, the Baltimore Ravens are giving up the 12th-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to TEs (+0.7). Of the 28 TEs with 25-plus targets, Strange is logging the sixth-most yards per reception (11.9) and the fourth-most yards per route run (2.10). Final Verdict: Start Kyle Pitts Starting Pitts always carries risk in an Atlanta Falcons offense that can look out of sorts at times. However, the Falcons are playing as underdogs against a high-octane Bengals offense in Week 9, which should lead to more passing opportunities. Additionally, between Pitts and Strange, Pitts has the higher touchdown upside. Strange has caught just one touchdown this season, and he has an unreliable role in the red zone, despite being in the better offensive environment. While the Jaguars are favored on the road against the shorthanded Ravens on Thursday Night Football, Strange may not see much usage. Jacksonville has three blowout wins this year, and Strange has scored fewer than 10 fantasy points in two of them. Both Pitts and Strange are viable starters for fantasy football managers in Week 9, but Pitts carries a higher ceiling. item.title: Sack-Prone Texas Offense Could Reignite Mizzou Pass Rush
item.description: Mizzou’s defense made it look relatively easy to get to the quarterback through the first half of the season. Over the past two weeks, however, the Tigers have struggled to generate the same pressure, giving the Texas offense an opportunity to exploit its pass-protection vulnerabilities. After 18 sacks through the first six games, Mizzou has managed just one over its last two contests. The Tigers have also totaled just three tackles for loss and seven quarterback hurries during that stretch. The recent production dip has dropped Mizzou to 11th in the SEC in total sacks. Despite the decrease, defensive ends Daeden Hopkins and Donta Simpson remain among the conference’s top five sack leaders with seven and six, respectively. Neither has maintained that production recently. Hopkins has gone without a sack in the last two games and recorded just one quarterback hurry. Simpson has added one sack and two hurries during that span. The bigger concern for the Tigers has been generating consistent pressure off the edge. Of the Tigers’ 19 sacks this season, nine have come from defensive tackles, 8.5 from defensive ends and 1.5 from linebacker Nic Rodriguez. Last season, Damon Wilson II and Zion Young combined for 15.5 sacks as edge rushers, providing a tandem of production that Mizzou has yet to replicate. Injuries have played a significant role. Hopkins has missed two games, Simpson was unavailable against Mississippi State and Darris Smith, who entered the season as the projected leader off the edge after recording four sacks in 2025, has appeared in just four games while playing fewer than 150 snaps. Smith did see an increased workload against Arkansas, recording 38 snaps, his most since playing 56 against Kansas. The lack of production hasn’t necessarily reflected a lack of creativity from defensive coordinator Corey Batoon and his staff. Against Arkansas, Mizzou mixed four- and five-man fronts with disguised coverages. On Trajen Greco’s interception, Hopkins started inside before crossing to the outside, helping both himself and Simpson generate pressure. . @TrajenGreco with the interception pic.twitter.com/SD0tkIS3ez — Mizzou Football (@MizzouFootball) November 1, 2026 Still, the numbers reflect the recent struggles. Mizzou’s sack percentage has fallen from 6.74% for the season, good for 10th in the SEC, to 3.54% over the last three weeks, ranking 12th in the conference. The matchup against Texas presents an opportunity to reverse this trend. The Longhorns have surrendered 24 sacks this season, the third-most in the SEC, while quarterback Arch Manning has been sacked 12 times over his last three games. Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz knows generating pressure against Manning will require more than simply sending extra rushers. “I think with every quarterback it can’t just be one one size fits all. You can’t just say we’re going to pressure him all game,” Drinkwitz said. “You can’t just play drop coverage because he does a great job with scrambling. So

item.title: Pat McAfee ‘acts irresponsibly’ & then plays victim says ex-ESPN star
item.description: Former ESPN sports media personality Katie Nolan has some strong words for Pat McAfee following the controversy surrounding his recent appearance at the University of Utah. Nolan believes the ESPN star wants the freedom to act however he chooses but struggles to accept the criticism that comes with being one of the most recognizable figures today in the media. Nolan questioned how McAfee handled the situation, arguing that he frequently presents himself as the target of unfair attacks despite his success. “The guy is winning in every sense of the word, and yet is constantly acting like the world is attacking him baselessly,” Nolan said. “He acts irresponsibly, but then wants everyone to be responsible for his emotional well-being, and to take care of him.” Nolan also compared McAfee’s reaction to the criticism she has received throughout her own career, including during her time in the Apple TV MLB broadcast booth. She suggested that McAfee would have difficulty dealing with the level of criticism she has experienced. item.title: Tobacco company got smoked by leaving secret recipes on a file share
item.description: Welcome once again to PWNED, where all of the security victims are self-owned. Today, we celebrate a company that makes a supremely unhealthy product having a supremely unhealthy security posture. Our tale of terrible data management, once again, comes courtesy of professional pen tester and red teamer Dahvid Schloss. Assigned to find flaws in the network of a tobacco company, Schloss stumbled onto some very poorly protected trade secrets. Schloss started by probing the network with tools like Metasploit, a popular open-source pen testing app. Surprisingly, the company’s Trend Micro antivirus did not issue an alert even as he was scanning the network for vulnerabilities. He compared the process to shooting a machine gun and having no one hear it. "I'm running through this environment, and I'm basically just using the loudest toys and tools you can imagine," he told The Register. It seemed as if the client simply didn't care much. "I'm feeling like there's not a whole lot of value that I'm providing here." Schloss then asked his boss what else he could do to make his findings more useful and compelling to the client. "My senior manager turns to me and goes 'Think about what is important to this organization. If it got leaked, how detrimental would it be to their business?'" Schloss said. "I’m thinking it’s a products company. Maybe their recipes." Schloss began searching for network file shares that allowed unauthenticated or anonymous access. After discovering an open share, he scanned it using the network mapping tool Nmap . The scan revealed that ports 139 and 445 were open , indicating that the system was running the Windows SMB file sharing protocol . Despite hosting sensitive IT and HR reco rds, this specific file share had no access restrictions and was completely exposed to every employee in the company. He clicked through the directories and found a folder named “confidential." He found files in there which were named recipe, the product name, the sub product name, and the date. He opened one file and discovered that it had information about how that tobacco product was made, including the weight and volume and what percentage of each chemical it had inside. The file was marked with red letters at the top that said "Confidential" and another set at the bottom that said "Do not share." “I think we found a smoking gun here. This is pretty bad,” Schloss said. He noted that anyone on the network could simply use Windows Explorer to find the file. Schloss downloaded the file, thinking he'd be able to show it to the company to prove that the data could be exfiltrated. But his manager asked him to delete the downloaded file, because it was such sensitive information that he shouldn't retain a copy. This would later harm his ability to show that it had ever existed at all. He then told the security team at the tobacco company what he had found, expecting them to lock down all the recipe files. But when he returned to the site the next morning, he

item.title: Blackburn duo doubts for West Ham game
item.description: Blackburn duo doubts for West Ham game Blackburn Rovers boss Tony Mowbray says Ryan Alebiosu will undergo a scan after suffering an injury against Stoke. Alebiosu was forced off in the game, with Blackburn now waiting to learn the extent of the problem. “He came into the team meeting limping pretty heavily,” Mowbray said. “I think he’ll probably have a scan. I don’t know; let’s wait to see it. “I don’t want to speculate; there’s every chance he could be out there on Saturday. But if the scan shows something specifically, he probably won’t be.” Tom Atcheson is also a doubt for the weekend’s game against West Ham after missing the Stoke game and the following training session because of a knock. Mowbray, though, played down the seriousness of the issue. “He’ll have to train tomorrow if he is going to be involved against West Ham,” he said. “I don’t think he’s a major concern for the medical department. You’d call it a minor niggle probably; if he’d played, he could have turned into a major niggle, and we didn’t think it was worth the risk of playing.”

item.title: Why Coachella Valley Lakers tip-off is significant to Acrisure Arena
item.description: Discussions about bringing the Los Angeles Lakers ' NBA G League team to the Coachella Valley began a couple years ago. But Acrisure Arena wasn't quote ready for that. The venue had been open less than two years, as the crown jewel home of the Coachella Valley Firebirds of the American Hockey League, and arena organizers were intensely focused on delivering on a promise of world-class concerts. The Palm Desert venue, which cost more than $300 million to build, has hosted the likes of Paul McCartney, the Eagles , Shania Twain, Harry Styles and Olivia Rodrigo, among others. On Friday, Acrisure Arena becomes an official home of basketball. The Coachella Valley Lakers' home opener against the Salt Lake City Stars brings the valley its first pro hoops team, and signals that the arena that arrived with concerts, shows and hockey in mind is growing into something even broader than perhaps originally envisioned. "It’s really a defining moment," said arena president John Page. "You really have to reflect back on the vision to build the arena here and bring this to the desert.” Tickets are still available for the opener against Salt Lake which tips off at 7 p.m. on Friday. Coachella Valley Lakers release schedule, will debut on Nov. 6 First-ever CV Lakers coach Alex Cerda unveils his plan for new team The Coachella Valley Lakers will play 24 home games at the arena during the 2026-27 season. The Lakers arrive in the valley having previously been the South Bay Lakers. They played their home games at UCLA Heath Training Center, a venue that housed just 750 seats. Page said that when the Lakers came calling, they were also looking at other venues in Southern California. But it seemed that they liked the venue in Palm Desert quite a bit and trusted arena organizers after the NBA club played pre-season basketball games here from 2023-25. So, to be clear, this is not the first basketball the arena will see. The Lakers are among the NBA teams, along with the Phoenix Suns , that have hosted pre-season games at the venue, and there has been high-level college basketball as well. Ahead of the season, Coachella Valley Lakers players are promising an exciting brand of basketball. "I think in the G League we're all trying to model our parent club," Syracuse grad and sharp-shooter Cole Swider said. "So, fans will see some of the same schemes as the Los Angeles Lakers. The play style is going to be very similar. The biggest difference is the pace in the G League is just insane. You're going to see a lot of athletes, a lot of speed, a lot of agility, so you'll see a fun brand of basketball." Last season, the South Bay Lakers averaged 122.3 points per game. Coachella Valley Lakers guard Chris Manon said that he believes the team will be one of the premier teams in the G League this season and forward AK Okereke said that there's a pull to play especially well in an effort to generate local fan support. "It's monumental, this first game, first home game, first game we've al

item.title: 'Hard pill to swallow': Bradley Braves women's basketball star out for season
item.description: PEORIA — Claire McDougall loves basketball. But unfortunately, the Bradley Braves guard/forward will spend her senior women's basketball season on the sidelines. The Washington native confirmed she is undergoing surgery to repair a torn ACL and meniscus on Nov. 23. The torn ACL is the same injury, to the same knee, McDougall suffered eight games into the 2025-26 season. Her injury this season came going up for a layup in an exhibition against North Central College on Oct. 19. "This time around I (tore my) ACL, meniscus," McDougall told the Journal Star on Thursday, Oct. 29. "And sprained some other ligaments as well. I honestly did not know right away. I didn't think it was possible for it to be the ACL again just because it was something so simple. It was also a two-footed routine layup, something that I do every single day. "This was actually the first thing I was allowed to do on the court. ... They got me in the next day and about 24 hours later, after it happened, I found out that my season was over again, so that stung." She had just made her return to the court and playing on Oct. 5. "I was just so grateful to be on the court again," McDougall said. "Basketball gives me a high that nothing else in life really gives me. Just the joy of being on the floor and it was something that I obviously hadn't felt in a while. It was a little overwhelming. I was just really grateful to be back because I love it. I love every second of it. "I love the grind. I love creating offense, cheering for my teammates, attacking the rim. I love everything about basketball. I love everything that it can give me." In eight games last season, McDougall averaged career bests in points (8.9) and rebounds (6.1). The former Washington All-State selection shot 62.2% from the field and played 22.1 minutes a game at the time of her initial knee injury in 2025-26. "A hard pill to swallow" McDougall says the most difficult aspect mentally is just coming to terms with the new reality of her life and it being a 'Hard pill to swallow.' "I've never had basketball taken away from me like this," McDougall said. "And it consumed me. In every every aspect of my life, if I wasn't playing basketball, I was coaching it or I was watching it. Basketball was my life and I didn't know who I was without it. "The hardest thing about it isn't even the pain because it is painful. But it's watching my teammates have so much fun and doing the thing that I loved when it just got stripped from me. Like that hurts because that's all I want to do is be out on the floor with them ... watching other people experience something that has been taken from me is probably just the hardest thing about it, honestly. I try to be a good teammate and supportive because at the end of the day, it's out of everyone's control. "God had a plan for me. And obviously in that period of my life, in this period of my life, it wasn't basketball. It isn't basketball. And so I just, I have to accept that reality." During the

item.title: Ohio State adding some major names to Oregon game guest
item.description: The Buckeyes are now onto Oregon. There’s no more time to reflect. It’s time to fix the issues and ensure this team wins out. No small task, Ohio State has tough opponents left on this schedule, and the players themselves have pointed towards the notion that these are now de-facto playoff games knowing they already have two losses. Returning back home this weekend also means recruiting opportunities, and the guest list for this weekend is impressive once again. Plenty of top targets making the trek from all over the country, here’s a rundown and the latest on some of those high-profile names set to be on campus come Saturday. Already looking ahead to the future recruiting cycles, Ohio State and every other top program for that matter are loving what they see from 2029 defesive back target James Allen . A 6-foot-3, 175 pound corneback out of Tampa, Florida, Allen is already boasting an impressive 50-plus offers to his name and rightfully so. The No. 3 player nationally and top cornerback in the 247Sports rankings, James has his pick of where he wants to go, and thus far Ohio State is very much in the mix for his services. Considered to be a top contender in his recruitment at least right now, it’s still important to note how much time is left before he makes a decision, but it’s the actions that go with his pro-Ohio State words that are exciting for this staff. Set to be on campus this weekend for the Oregon game, the Buckeyes will have a major opportunity to continue showing Allen why Columbus is the place to be for his college career and development. Sure to roll out the red carpet treatment for him this weekend, these are the types of visits that can have a player leaving even further impressed with all that the program has to offer, and that’s the goal for Ohio State. One of the premier guests set to be on site this weekend, the Buckeyes are thrilled to be playing host to Allen and will make his time worth the while. 🌰 https://t.co/HYfzzVMPqG — James Allen (@allenj2010) November 4, 2026 Seeing certain names resurface over and over shows how the staff views them, and that’s been the case with Georgia native John Matthews . A 6-foot, 175 pound receiver prospect, Matthews was offered by the Buckeyes in late July of this summer and since then the staff has remained in close contact. Other notable programs such as Notre Dame offering after Ohio State, it’s fair to say he’s been one of the rising players in the 2028 class, and Cortez Hankton would like Columbus to be his eventual home with what he’s seen. The No. 424 player nationally and 61st best at his position per the 247Sports Composite, Matthews may have an under-the-radar ranking compared to what most Ohio State receiver targets have, but the offer list and approval from this staff are all you need to know about the caliber of player he is. The good news, the Buckeyes are in a solid position and this weekend further confirms that. Making the trek for the Oregon game, Matthews will be in town

item.title: Could the 49ers make a deal with the Texans again for a defensive lineman?
item.description: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 04: Defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins #98 of the Houston Texans and defensive end Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Houston Texans celebrate a defensive stop during the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Dallas Cowboys on October 4, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers and the Houston Texans have been involved in some business over the past few years. Back in 2024, the 49ers dealt a seventh-round pick for defensive tackle Maliek Collins in a move that worked out for them for a year. Collins was a solid pass-rusher and went on to sign with the Cleveland Browns, where he’s found even more success, recently signing an extension. They’ve also traded seventh-round picks to the Texans for defensive tackle Khalil Davis and offensive lineman Jarrett Patterson in separate trades. Now, could it be time for a fourth deal over the past two years? Heading into the trade deadline, the 49ers already made a splash move, landing DeForest Buckner for a 2027 fourth-round pick to slot in as their new starting defensive tackle. Following that, the 49ers are still actively looking for a pass rusher and a wide receiver, and one of those needs could be filled with a minor trade with the Texans. CBS Sports mocked a trade between the 49ers and Texans for veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, with the two sides swapping sixth and seventh-round picks in the deal. “The Niners have already given their defensive line a boost by trading for DeForest Buckner, and they should welcome Nick Bosa back into the fold soon, if not this week coming off their bye,” CBS Sports’s Jared Dubin wrote. “But they’re still just 21st in the NFL in pressure rate, according to Tru Media, and they have been dealing with injuries along the defensive front all season. Adding another capable rotational player off the edge could give them an extra boost ahead of a potential playoff run.” In the deal, the 49ers are receiving a 2027 seventh-round pick, while sending out a 2028 sixth-round pick. Clowney has been a name that has popped up in trade conversations this week, as he’s played under 40 percent of the defensive snaps for the Texans and is 33 years old. The 49ers currently have a draft pick in every round but the fourth in the 2027 NFL Draft after the Buckner trade, so they could swap sixths and sevenths this year. But if they’re asked to move a 2028 pick and get a 2027 in return, the deal could make even more sense. And it could make sense for Houston as well, as they currently don’t have a 2028 sixth-round pick. If the 49ers are to look for a pass rusher and a wide receiver, at least one of those moves will have to be cheap. San Francisco doesn’t have any projected compensatory picks coming their way this offseason. So two trades could mean two additional picks from their 2027 war chest gone, leaving them with just four draft picks in the class. A move

item.title: Brock Bowers dominates as a wide receiver
item.description: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-33 win at the New York Jets on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick had seven catches for 92 yards and a score. According to Next Gen Stats, six of his catches, for 87 yards, were when hew as lined up as a wide receiver. It’s the most by a tight end in the NFL in 10 years. He is a wild weapon. And, yes, his contract talks next offseason are going to be very interesting. Jackson Powers-Johnson: The second-round pick remained on the bench for the third straight game. He is now a backup and he did warm up at just center Sunday, so he may not even be a guard anymore. D.J. Glaze: The third-round pick started at right tackle as usual and performed well. Tommy Eichenberg: The fifth-round pick from Ohio State played 22 defensive snaps and had his ups and downs. He also played 26 snaps on special teams, which was tied for the team high. Dylan Laube: The sixth-round pick made a huge impact with a 95-yard kick return for a touchdown in the second quarter. The Raiders may have lost the game without it. It was the first kick return for a score in the league this season and the Raiders’ first in 15 years. Laube is, by far, the kickoff leader in the NFL at 34.1 average. He has a 2.8 yard lead over any other returner. Only four players have finished a season wit ha higher average with the most recent coming in 1970.

item.title: Why does the BYU-Utah rivalry game trigger such deep emotions? We asked a sports psychology professor
item.description: Eliza Anderson, Deseret News As you’re settling in Saturday morning for the BYU versus Utah kickoff, consider a question that fans have likely been asking since the gladiators battled in the Roman Colosseum over 2,000 years ago: “Why are many of us so emotionally invested in the outcome of a game being played by young athletes that most don’t know?” There’s no rational answer to that query. Unless you’re a gambler, the final score in Saturday’s Cougars/Utes contest won’t affect your bankbook. The Big Game results won’t move gas prices. Taxes aren’t going away. And your golf handicap? Sorry, it stays the same. But forget rationality. The outcome of the annual Red-and-Blue rivalry game matters deeply to many of us. When the final horn blows, legions of fans sporting one particular color will be celebrating. And legions wearing the other color will be grumbling. And the number of postgame “celebrators” and the “grumblers” will be almost evenly split, according to a new poll released Thursday. When 786 Utahns were asked in a recent Y2 Analytics survey which Utah school they usually root for, BYU edged out the University of Utah 37% to 34%, with the remainder of respondents claiming support for other teams or no team from the Beehive State. But when all participating in the survey were required to pick a side — BYU or Utah — roughly 52% of respondents sided with the Utes, compared to 48% for the Cougs. Why do we care so much about a college football game? The Deseret News reached out to Matt Moore, a sports and exercise psychology professor at the University of Utah who has worked with both schools, to explore why many care so deeply about the annual Cougars-Utes football game. Moore’s simple answer: It’s vital to many Utahns’ identity. “We are social beings that walk through this world with identities: ‘I work here,’ or ‘I go to school here,’ or ‘I live here,’ or ‘I own this,’ or ‘I cheer for this team,’ or ‘I belong to this faith/religion’,” he wrote in an email. Psychology’s Social Identity Theory comes into play when examining fans of both teams, he added. The teams we attach our personal identity to become part of the larger “Us” — our school, family, faith tradition, history and community. “That is why fans say, ‘ We won,’ rather than, ‘ They won,’ even though 99% of fanbases haven’t even stepped foot on the field or inside a locker room,” explained Moore. “Team success can bring genuine pride, belonging, and joy. And, by contrast, team failure can feel like ‘We lost,’ or ‘We suck.’ That ‘identity” piece to our human experience is huge — and sports play, and will always play, a role in that.” The BYU-Utah rivalry: Unique elements While many spirited college sports rivalries are fueled across dividing lines such as neighboring states (think Oklahoma vs. Texas) or private-vs-public (Duke vs. North Carolina), the BYU-Utah rivalry is unique because both fanbases exist within the same interconnected social world. “Families, workplaces, neighborhoods,

Joe Burrow (at ATL) Burrow has been dealing as the season-long QB2 (26.2 PPG), generating +0.23 EPA per dropback (QB5). He is lighting up box scores through the air, leading the league in passing yards per game (302) and passing touchdowns per game (2.9). Cincinnati is leaning all the way into his arm, operating with a league-high 66% neutral pass rate (first). (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports) That aggressive approach meets an Atlanta defense allowing 16.3 half PPR points per game to quarterbacks (23rd), where recent signal-callers like Tyler Huntley (24.0 points) and Caleb Williams (16.5 points) have put up functional days. The Bengals head in as 3-point road favorites with an implied team total of 27.25 points (sixth). 2. Josh Allen (at MIN) Allen's 28.2 fantasy points per game is currently ahead of the all-time fantasy record at QB (Lamar Jackson, 2024). He's done so without DJ Moore for half of the season. Moore was used properly last week with unlimited run-away routes, and then Dalton Kincaid found space downfield in multi-TE sets. It's a great formula. (Chart by Hayden Winks/Yahoo Sports) The Vikings have been by far the best fantasy QB defense, however, allowing just 10.4 fantasy points per game. That's insane. Truly. They haven't faced an elite dual-threat QB this season, though. Allen will be blitzed at a career-high rate, most likely. He's the QB5 in EPA per dropback against the blitz (+0.07), but that is far lower than on non-blitzes (+0.21, QB1). When blitzed, Allen has a 3.4% scramble rate compared to a 9% scramble rate when not blitzed. It's possible the Bills run a bit more often because of the pressure, as opposing offenses to Minnesota only pass 45% of the time in neutral situations (31st). Buffalo enters as 3.5-point road favorites carrying an implied team total of 25.0 points (11th). It would make sense for Allen's fantasy output to take a hit here. 3. Brock Purdy (vs. LV) We'll see if Mike Evans (Achilles) can return, but it doesn't sound like Deebo Samuel Sr. will be back. Purdy has been surgical as fantasy's QB4 (21.7 PPG), leading all qualified quarterbacks with +0.31 EPA per dropback (QB1). item.title: Triple injury boost for Swansea before Blues test
item.description: Stephen Welsh has started 13 of Swansea's 14 league games so far this season [PA] Swansea City have received a major fitness boost after influential centre-back Stephen Welsh was cleared of serious injury. Swansea feared the Scotland international had suffered knee ligament damage following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Tuesday's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth. But scans have revealed Welsh has no significant problem, meaning he may even be able to play some part at Birmingham City on Saturday. There is more positive news from the treatment room going into the weekend, with wingers Moussa Yeo and Eom Jisung fit to return against Chris Davies' in-form Blues side. However, midfielder Stephen Eustaquio will again be absent due to a groin problem and Melker Widell is out with a minor hamstring injury which meant he was withdrawn at half-time at Fratton Park. "Welshy's scan is clear. It's just really a bad knock so there's nothing major," said Swansea head coach Vitor Matos. "We will still assess if he will be available for Saturday, but it's not a bad injury. It's just a knock that is really, really painful." Matos says a decision is yet to be taken on whether Welsh, 26, will join up with Scotland in the international break which follows the Birmingham game. Stephen Eustaquio scored before coming off injured during last weekend's 4-0 win over Blackburn [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Eustaquio, who came off injured during last weekend's win over Blackburn, has been withdrawn from Canada duty, with Swansea hoping the former Porto player may be fit for their game against West Bromwich Albion on Saturday, 21 November. Widell is expected back for the Baggies' visit, while Yeo returns this weekend having missed Swansea's past three matches with a hamstring issue and Eom is back in contention after a knock suffered against Blackburn last weekend. Matos revealed Ben Cabango did not train in the lead-up to Portsmouth because of a fitness issue, hence he was on the bench before coming on to replace Welsh, but Swansea's captain is available for Birmingham. "In this moment unfortunately we are having a few knocks and that creates a little bit of instability regarding the starting XI and the availability of players," Matos added. "You need to learn how to deal with the situations and that's it. It's hard to manage, but we will find a way of course." item.title: Derrick White on how Boston Celtics weathered strong second half to beat Bucks
item.description: Too often for the fans of the Boston Celtics, a big lead gets built up in the first half of a game, only to see it wither on the vine in the second, the team falling to an otherwise inferior foe. But that did not happen in the Celtics' 109-102 win vs. the Milwaukee Bucks at TD Garden on Wednesday (Nov. 4) evening. Instead, the Celtics found a way to survive a red-hot Bucks squad on a night Boston struggled to get their offense going in the game's third quarter. "I think they started making a lot of shots up to pressure," said Boston point guard Derrick White of how the Celtics weathered that particular storm. "The ball pressure was high, but then they were also in that deep drop with the bigs, so it was in between of do you want to shoot that runner every time down the court, or do you want to work it around." "And they were top-locking, so they changed that a little bit and caught us on our heels to start," added the Colorado native. "I think down the stretch, a lot of guys made big plays," continued White. "(Paul George) hit a big shot. Baylor (Scheierman), big rebounds." "Neemi (Queta) protecting the paint (and) rebounding; Sam (Hauser) was a little bit everywhere, so (we) just found a way, made big plays, and found a way to get a win." item.title: Is a sports media blue wave coming, too?
item.description: Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect This originally appeared in Thursday morning’s edition of The A Block, Awful Announcing’s daily newsletter with the latest sports media news, commentary, and analysis. Sign up here to be the first to know everything happening in the sports media world each day. Only a fool would try to extrapolate what happened on election night and tell you what’s next. While I am a fool, I will refrain from doing so. Instead, I’ll ponder a question. Will the ripple effects from Tuesday’s Blue Tsunami make their way to the sports media world? I ask because we’re only two years removed from seeing how shifting political headwinds can affect the industry and its content. This political outcome didn’t happen overnight. We can debate the specific reasons, but the person at the center of this seismic change is Donald Trump, and America’s desire to pull away or move past him has been months in the making. I think about that when I look around at the state of the sports media world and how some of the things he affected or influenced are already fraying at the edges. The Vibe Shift That Wasn’t Remember the Trump Vibe Shift ? That sense that, as David Wallace-Wells put it , “the country would be moving MAGA-ward — both in politics and beyond it.” We saw it in the ways sports leagues changed their policies and even their histories to appease a new cultural worldview. We saw it with the mainstream acceptance of Barstool Sports and Pat McAfee’s world domination . LIV Golf’s presumed domination thanks to Saudi backing and Trump approval. The ascension of prediction markets and gambling’s complete infiltration of sports media . Some have argued we’ve seen it in the choices companies like ESPN make about which talent gets featured and which gets let go . Whether because of his TACO tendencies or the cold, hard realities of the American legal system, we’ve since learned there was no real reason for any company, network, or league to fall in line with any of that. In fact, as his popularity waned and he became radioactive, the only logical answer was to break cleanly with Trump and his broken vision of America. And slowly but surely, many of those shifts have started to reverse, with some already running their course. On Wednesday, it was reported that LIV, once seemingly destined to rule the golf world, had lost its critical funding and was, in essence, dead. There was a certain kind of harmony to that news dropping the day after the election. The Cracks Are Already Visible We’ve spent a lot of time talking about Pat McAfee and College GameDay recently, trying to suss out that feeling that, despite its impossible-to-ignore success, something feels decidedly off about the show’s current version. I don’t want to draw a direct line between McAfee and Trump (although they’re clearly two peas in a pod ). However, while McAfee draws an audience and commands attention, there’s also no denying he’s overextended his welcome with everyone be

item.title: Microplastics may be changing the colour of the Pacific Ocean
item.description: Fishing nets make up a large part of the debris in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch Ocean Voyages Institute/ZUMA Wire/Shutterstock The sea around the Great Pacific Garbage Patch is changing colour, and microplastics may be to blame. The Great Pacific Garbage Patch (GPGP), located roughly midway between Hawaii and California, covers around 1.6 million square kilometres and is thought to contain nearly 80,000 tonnes of plastic debris, carried there by ocean currents. Read more How worried should you be about microplastics? Near the surface of the ocean in parts of the garbage patch, microplastic densities may reach up to 17 milligrams per cubic litre. Advertisement While most concern about the vast patch has focused on its impact on sea life and environmental health, three separate datasets have shown distinct colour changes in the ocean itself. Other recent research has found that the world’s oceans are generally darkening for a variety of reasons, including agricultural runoff and phytoplankton growth. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter “The ocean’s colour is created from the interaction of sunlight with seawater and all the things contained in it, and therefore the colour is indicative of the ocean’s content,” says Shea Cheatham at the University of Bergen, Norway. The unique circulation patterns that have created the garbage patch have also created an area much more likely to experience the kind of microplastic accumulation needed to be detectable from space, she says. Cheatham and her colleagues analysed three satellite datasets collected between 2002 and 2022. The data showed that parts of the GPGP saw an approximately 10 per cent increase in blue light and a 2 to 4 per cent increase in green light over the 20-year period. Not all of the satellites agreed on the extent of the blue and green brightening, which together create the colour cyan, but all found that some brightening had occurred. To try to work out what was causing the brightening, the researchers used computer simulations to test how the ocean’s colour would theoretically change if microscopic pieces of plastic were added to the water. They also simulated how the ocean’s colour would change from natural things, like more or different micro-algae and other material. Should we give up on recycling plastic? Globally, only 14 per cent of the plastic we use is recycled – but some countries achieve higher rates and new technologies could change the picture drastically “We found that brightening of the water in both blue and green light is rarely produced by natural changes,” says Cheatham. “When we included microplastic particles in our simulations, this pattern we saw near the Great Pacific Garbage Patch of brightening in both blue and green light became more than four times as likely.” Microplastic particles, in contrast to most natural contributors to ocean colour, do not absorb very much light, she says, but scatter light strongly. “This means that as
