item.title: Long climb to the top: Inside Guilderland girls' tennis' historic state semifinal run
item.description: Guilderland tennis teammates Meghan Uzzilia, left, and Angela Li during the Section 2 finals against Niskayuna on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, in Schenectady, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) GUILDERLAND CENTER - Guilderland's grind to reach the top of the Section 2 Class AA girls' tennis hierarchy proved to be a methodical push up from the middle of the pack. But longtime Lady Dutch Coach Deb Murray had an inkling heading into this fall that her 2026 squad was ready to break through. "I knew that this would be the year to do it if we were going to make it happen," Murray said. "I have five seniors that have been with me since they were 11 and 12 years old. It is an exceptional group. They have been committed to the game and with me on the varsity. They play in the seven main positions. Last year, we were good. We beat Saratoga Springs during the regular season and lost to them in the final." Guilderland not only edged Shaker 5-4 for the sectional title, but has since won two more matches to advance to the Division I state semifinals Friday at the United States Tennis Association's Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing. Guilderland faces Section 1 champion Horace Greeley at 9:30 a.m. If the Section 2 champion prevails, it would compete in the title match in the afternoon. "I have been waiting for something like this since I joined the team," said senior Angela Li, who became a member of the varsity roster in eighth grade. "I never expected it. I have played tennis all my life and Guilderland tennis gave me a new opportunity. I have really enjoyed it on this team." "I am excited. No matter how well we do, we got there," Guilderland senior Meghan Uzzilia said. "This is the first time a Guilderland team has done this and there are also not many teams from around the state that have been this far." Guilderland's first sectional title in 16 years was followed up by a 7-0 triumph over Queensbury for the right to represent Section 2 in the state Division I tournament. They followed with a 6-1 regional victory over Section 3 champion Fayetteville-Manlius. Players say they were motivated to win the title for Murray because of all the work she's put in through the years. "It meant a lot to us to get her that win," Uzzilia said. "We had never been to regionals before and it was nice to play new people." "We were all really happy to win it. We felt we deserved it after what happened last year, coming in second at sectionals," Li said. "This is the best team Guilderland has had in a while now. It is a great opportunity to be on this team now." The last time Guilderland captured a sectional team title in 2010, there was no team state championship event to compete in. "Because we were so close last year, we knew we had to pull this off this year," Uzzilia said. "Our lineup pretty much stayed the same and we have a pretty strong team. I had a lot of confidence going into the season. I really thought we would take the whole thing."

item.title: The Chiefs have lost their fastball against quality opponents
item.description: (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images One of my favorite skills Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes possesses is his ability to be one step faster than any player chasing him. It doesn’t matter if it’s a defensive tackle or a cornerback; he’ll outrace them to the sideline to get his throw off. It’s magic. That ability has seemingly rubbed off on the Chiefs over the years. Think about how many times we’ve seen this team be so much better than the opposition. It doesn’t really matter who the opponent is on the opposing sideline. The Chiefs just seem to find a way. It’s that Mahomes Magic. I miss it. Things changed last year. The team couldn’t find that extra gear early on, especially against the quality opponents on the schedule. The Chiefs’ one-score sorcery evolved into one-score nightmares. The entire season was a disaster from start to finish. This year would be different. It certainly felt different in the first month. The Chiefs sprinted to a 5-0 start. The vibes were generally positive. Things were back on track. Everything seemed to flip on a dime. I’m not sure exactly when it happened, but one play against the Seattle Seahawks sticks in my mind that I haven’t been able to shake. Nick Emmanwori put the athleticism on display to put the pressure on Mahomes 😤 KCvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GJtsfssHa9 — NFL (@NFL) October 26, 2026 In the second quarter, the Chiefs line up rookie running back Emmett Johnson behind Mahomes in the pistol formation. Mahomes fakes a pitch to Johnson to the right and rolls to his left, and he has to beat a defender to his spot to get the throw off as he had done so many times before. A step faster than every defender, right? Not this time. He has met his match. Safety Nick Emmanwori chased down Mahomes from behind and forced a bad throw to Jalen Royals, resulting in a Seahawks interception. The Chiefs were trailing 3-0 at the time. The Seahawks took a 10-0 lead on the next drive and never looked back. Was that the moment the bad vibes returned? It’s hard to say. The Chiefs didn’t immediately follow that game with another terrible performance. They were leading 24-13 entering the fourth quarter on the road against the Broncos. That’s a game they should win. But they didn’t. They fell short. Again. It’s becoming a trend, the kind I never thought we would see under head coach Andy Reid and Mahomes. This team just doesn’t seem to have that ability to keep quality opponents at arm’s reach any longer. The Chiefs were 16-7 from 2022-2024 in the regular season with Patrick Mahomes as the starter against teams that finished the year at or above .500. They have gone just 3-9 against that same caliber of opponents over the past two seasons. They went from the second-best winning percentage in the NFL from 2022-2024 against opponents who finished with at least a .500 record to the team with the 13th-worst record in the league over the past two seasons aga

item.title: Stats Corner: Who’s still Alive in MWC Title Race
item.description: As we reach the final stretch of conference play, there is still a lot to play for in the Mountain West: the conference title, bowl positioning, the Commander-in-Chief’s Trophy and, remarkably, likely a first time champion. Neither New Mexico nor North Dakota State has ever won an MWC title. Air Force earned a share of the 2004 regular-season crown and reached the 2015 title game; Wyoming won the regular season in 2001 and made the title game in 2016, both lost the title game. No matter who lifts the trophy next month, history will likely be made. This week on Stats Corner, we look at the probability of each team still in the conference title race and what each needs to happen over the final weeks. Five teams are mathematically eliminated: Nevada, San Jose State, Hawaii, Northern Illinois, and UTEP. The Huskies and Miners won’t be going bowling; Hawaii needs to win out just to reach six wins, with roughly a 9% chance of getting there. #1) New Mexico 4-0 in MWC — 66% Chance of Winning the Conference Remaining games and win probabilities: @ Nevada — 81.0% vs. UNLV — 81.5% @ Wyoming — 88.8% vs. Air Force — 81.3% The Lobos’ last conference title came in 1964, as WAC co-champions and they’re nationally ranked for the first time in school history. At 7-1 they are guaranteed a bowl berth, with an outside shot at the playoff picture, they need Boise State to lose. They’re favored in all four remaining games; win out and they host the conference title game. Crucially, the Lobos already beat North Dakota State, giving them the head-to-head tiebreaker over the only other two-loss contender. #2) North Dakota State 4-2 in MWC — 20% Chance Remaining games and win probabilities: @ Hawaii — 63.9% vs. Northern Illinois — 95.0% @ San Jose State — 74.5% The Bison have two conference losses (UNLV and New Mexico), so why are they second? Two reasons. First, they’re heavy favorites in their final three games none harder than a road trip to Honolulu. Second, UNLV plays Wyoming this week, so one of the one-loss teams is guaranteed a second loss. NDSU has made serious noise in its first FBS and MWC season, and like New Mexico, has secured its bowl eligibility at six wins. But the math is stark: to take the regular-season title, the Bison need the Lobos to lose three of their final four the head-to-head tiebreaker leaves no other path. #3) UNLV 3-1 in MWC — 8% Chance Remaining games and win probabilities: vs. Wyoming — 79.2% @ New Mexico — 18.5% @ San Jose State — 68.8% vs. Nevada — 70.1% For a team with conference title and playoff aspirations, this season has been a bit of a disappointment. But the path exists: win out which means winning at New Mexico, the only game in which they’d be an underdog and then hope the Lobos stumble elsewhere. With only one conference loss (against Air Force) and a win over North Dakota State, a three-way tie at the top, excluding the Falcons, would break in the Rebels’ favor. #4) Air Force 3-2 in MWC — 4% Chance Remaining games and win pro

item.title: Barcelona offered Ruud Nijstad hope as FC Twente chief Erik ten Hag talks transfers
item.description: ALKMAAR - Ruud Nijstad of FC Twente celebrates the victory after the Eredivisie match between AZ Alkmaar and FC Twente at the AFAS Stadium on October 25, 2026, in Alkmaar, the Netherlands. WART BRINKERHOF / ANP (Photo by ANP via Getty Images) | ANP via Getty Images FC Twente’s technical director Erik ten Hag has offered Barcelona hope of landing young defender Ruud Nijstad in the future. The Dutch club have already acknowledged interest from Barca , while Nijstad has admitted he’d love to play alongside Pau Cubarsi. The defender signed a contract extension last summer, but Ten Hag admits his club will have to make big sales. “Every club in the Netherlands has to sell every year. You are the Eredivisie,” he told Goedemorgen Eredivisie. “If you want to remain competitive in Europe, you need a certain budget. But to maintain that budget, you simply have to sell. That applies to FC Twente, but also to Ajax, PSV, and Feyenoord.” Ten Hag also made it clear that Barcelona aren’t the only club keen on Nijstad and that there has been plenty of interest in the defender. “He is a very great talent, who came into the team last season. He is still very young, but he does so in a very self-assured way. It is a pleasure to work with that boy, Quite a few clubs from the top of Europe have come forward. I think that is only a good thing,” he added. “Several clubs from the top eight in Europe have made concrete offers. But he simply made a very conscious choice to play for FC Twente this season. It is also particularly nice that he very consciously chose to stay with Twente for at least another year. Maybe even longer, but in any case, this season.” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has admitted he’s keen to sign another defender, although it remains to be seen if the club will move in January or wait until the summer.

item.title: Cubs free agent target: Freddy Peralta
item.description: Right-hander Freddy Peralta was widely assumed to be a Cubs trade target last summer while he was with the Mets. He’d had several good seasons pitching for Craig Counsell in Milwaukee, likely enough to recommend him. But Peralta was pretty bad in 22 starts with the Mets: 4.99 ERA, 1.478 WHIP, 17 home runs allowed in 113.1 innings. That included losing twice to the Cubs. So the Cubs instead traded for two other members of the Mets rotation and Peralta went to the Rays, where he pitched in the World Series — and was also very good in the 10 regular-season starts he made in Tampa Bay, posting a 3.25 ERA and 1.012 WHIP, more in line with his Milwaukee numbers The reason this happened is simple. The Rays figured out how to fix him: [Jorge] Moncada, the Rays’ bullpen coach since 2023 after a lengthy stint in their system as a pitching coach and coordinator, dug into video of Peralta when he was at his best for Milwaukee last September and when he was at his worst in his final starts as a Met in July. Soon enough, Moncada noticed something: Last season, Peralta exclusively pitched out of the stretch. This season, he was going through an elaborate windup, hands over his head, with the bases empty. So he posed a question to his newest pupil as the meeting drew to a close: Which is more comfortable? “He said, ‘I always feel comfortable pitching out of the stretch,'” Moncada said. “So we were like, ‘Go with what makes you most comfortable,’ and he went back.” From there, the Rays instituted further modifications. They had Peralta move to the third-base side of the rubber and widen his stance. They told him to speed up his delivery. They gave him a drill package to incorporate into his preparation to generate more strength from his legs. In one of the drills, Peralta straps a 3D belt around his waist and Moncada pulls it so he feels the weight in his backside. The modified routine, Moncada explained, set the foundation for Peralta to create better momentum toward the plate. His arm angle was raised slightly. His average arm extension rose a fraction. I quoted quite a bit there — and there’s more, go to the link — mainly to give a prime example of how other teams’ pitching infrastructure is so far superior to the Cubs’. I wonder, had the Cubs actually been able to trade for Peralta, whether they would have been able to figure these things out and implement them the way they were in Tampa Bay. I’ll continue to maintain that Jed Hoyer ought to fire pitching coach Tommy Hottovy, VP of pitching strategy Tyler Zombro, and the rest of the pitcher coaches and start over. How much worse could it be? Nevertheless, it does appear that Peralta is back to the way he pitched in Milwaukee, and that should be something that should attract the Cubs to signing him, especially with his long history with Counsell. Peralta is 30 and will turn 31 in June. MLBTR says he’s worth a five-year, $110 million deal, which would be for his ages 31-35 seasons. I think such a deal would be

item.title: Carlos Prates manager: UFC ‘a little upset’ with Islam Makhachev after UFC 336 withdrawal
item.description: Carlos Prates | Ishika Samant, Getty Images Carlos Prates is not fighting Islam Makhachev for the UFC welterweight title, news that caught all parties involved by surprise. Instead of getting his shot at the undisputed belt, Prates battles Michael Morales for an interim title in the co-main event of UFC 336 on Jan. 30 in Toronto. Prates’ manager Lucas Lutkus told MMA Fighting that Prates was promised a shot at the 170-pound gold minutes after knocking out former champion Jack Della Maddalena in the main event of UFC Perth in May and three months prior to Makhachev’s successful title defense against Ian Machado Garry. Prates was offered the January date against Makhachev following UFC 330, and immediately agreed to it, a claim that was confirmed by UFC CEO Dana White. “Islam said at the press conference that he wanted to fight before Ramadan,” Lutkus said, “And the UFC had already told us that the plan was to have this fight at the first numbered event in January. ‘Get ready for that date.’” Makhachev previously stated he was determined to enter the cage one more time before Feb. 7, when Ramadan begins. “Bro, we have to fight before Ramadan. 100 percent. January, end of the year, I have to fight,” Makhachev said on Aug. 16 . “Because I’m not like 20-something, I’m 34 years old and I have to fight soon as possible because I’m not cutting much weight, I don’t have any big injuries, just have to maybe double check my nose, that’s it.” The scenario changed on Oct. 20, when the UFC called Lutkus to inform them Makhachev said he would not be able to fight in January. “The UFC called me last Tuesday and said, ‘Islam is out,’” Lutkus said. “I asked if it was an injury, and they said Islam hadn’t given them a reason. He had only said he wouldn’t be ready for January, and they weren’t going to break their promise that Carlos’ next fight would be for the title, so they would have Carlos fight Morales for the belt.” “I don’t think even the UFC really knows what happened,” he continued, “because Islam comes out of the fight with Ian Garry, takes the microphone, and says, ‘I’m going to fight before Ramadan.’ His coaches say Prates is the most deserving contender, too. There was even a quick encounter backstage after the fight in Philadelphia, and everything was understood. Makhachev said this past weekend that Prates and Morales should fight each other to determine “a true worthy contender.” “This talk from Islam about there being so many contenders doesn’t hold up,” Lutkus said. “He might be saying that now, but he’s changing his tune from what he said right after the fight in Philadelphia. He always said Carlos deserved it and that Morales wasn’t fighting. Anyway, something made him change his mind. I’m not naive enough to think Islam Makhachev is afraid to fight Carlos Prates, but something made him change his mind. And as far as I know, he hasn’t explained it to the UFC. item.title: 2026 Phillies report cards: J.T. Realmuto
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 01: Philadelphia catcher J.T. Realmuto (10) reacts during the Philadelphia Phillies versus the Atlanta Braves in game 3 of the National League Wild Card Series on October 1st, 2026 at Truist Park in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jim Morrison was a controversial singer for the band The Doors in the late 1960’s. Controversial because, well, you have Google and can probably look it up for yourself. Morrison wrote a song called “The End” which, if you’ve ever seen Apocalypse Now , you are more than familiar with. It’s a super long song that starts with these lyrics “This is the end/My only friend, the end”. It’s a great song, one that would take you back to the time and feel of music in the 1960’s and one of the better ones in The Doors’ catalogue of music. Why do I bring this up in a season ending report card of J.T. Realmuto. Because it’s time to face the music. We are nearing the end of Realmuto’s career and 2026 never made that fact more clear. Even after re-signing him, something I’d argue was necessary if too expensive, the team needs to have a contingency better than what they had the past two years. What went right If we’re looking for any positives to bring to light about Realmuto’s season, one could be that he looks to have staunched the bleeding he had with his defense. He had descended to being considered one of the worse framers in the game to getting himself back to at least being average. He was outstanding at challenging calls with the ABS system in place, his 81% overturned the highest among all starting catchers. Did he make those challenges enough? No. Would it have mattered? Probably not much. He was very good at knowing when to make those challenges that would help his team in certain situations. His arm strength is still a weapon, as is the pop time with which he can get rid of a baseball. What went wrong In 2026, there were 35 catchers in the game that logged at least 230 plate appearance as a catcher. Of those 35, only four had a worse wRC+ than Realmuto’s 68 wRC+. If you wanted to zoom the lens out a little more, there were 336 hitters at any position that had a least 230 plate appearances on the season. Realmuto’s 68 wRC+ was tied for 310th with four others at that same total. Not only is it fair to say he was a bad hitter for being a catcher, it’s fair to say that he was one of the worst hitters in the game – period. There have been some arguments that he ran into some bad batted ball luck. Can whoever makes that argument look at a lot of his under the hood numbers and say with a straight face that there was bad batted ball luck involved? I’m not sure anyone can. His spot in the lineup was a near black hole and there was just no way to get out of it. Final grade: D Realmuto just wasn’t that good last year, meaning he earns a grade that reflects that. This isn’t some kind of reflection on his career. He’s had a career that

item.title: Report – Atletico Madrid is targeting Arsenal star
item.description: Report – Atletico Madrid is targeting Arsenal star Mikel Merino has become an important member of the Arsenal squad, and his versatility and goalscoring ability make him an attractive option for clubs across Europe. It is therefore not entirely surprising that he has been linked with a move away from the Emirates Stadium, with Spanish side Atletico Madrid reportedly interested in signing him. Originally a midfielder, Merino has shown that he can also make an impact in attacking positions for both club and country . Even when deployed in his natural midfield role, his ability to arrive in dangerous areas and contribute goals makes him a valuable player. Arsenal signed the Spaniard to strengthen their midfield, but his contribution has extended beyond that original purpose. He has become an important option for Mikel Arteta, with his goals helping the Gunners make progress in recent times. Atletico Madrid add Merino to their plans Atletico have reportedly been monitoring Merino and are impressed by what they have seen from him. His qualities and experience appear to have made him an appealing target as the La Liga side considers potential additions to its squad. According to Fichajes , Merino has emerged as one of the players Atletico want to bring to the club. The report suggests he is among their main targets in the coming weeks, with the Spanish side keen to explore the possibility of bringing him back to La Liga. The report also claims Atletico will attempt to lure him away from North London, where he has struggled to play several matches . They could see an opportunity to convince him that a move would offer a fresh start and a chance to play more regularly. (Photo by Gabriel Kuchta/Getty Images) Arsenal face a decision over their midfielder Arsenal have no desire to lose Merino or any of their key players, particularly given the contribution he has made since arriving. His versatility gives Arteta useful options, and replacing his combination of midfield quality and attacking threat would not necessarily be straightforward. However, the Gunners also understand that every player has a price. Merino may consider his future if he cannot secure regular opportunities as a starter, making his situation one worth monitoring as Atletico’s reported interest develops. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: BVB podcast with nutritionist: „Cocoa and kebabs? Better than you think!“
item.description: BVB podcast with nutritionist: „Cocoa and kebabs? Better than you think!“ Sophie Kaltenbach has been at BVB since January 2025, initially as a performance nutritionist at the youth academy and, since July 2025, as a sports nutritionist. Her role is to support players from the U9s to the U23s on their journey and show them how the right nutrition can help their development and performance. Rather than strict meal plans or bans, the focus is on building an understanding of food and how it affects the body. To do this, Sophie runs workshops and presentations for the young players, organises group cooking sessions and offers individual nutrition coaching. But what does that mean in everyday life? What should children eat when they have training straight after school? Which snacks are best before and after exercise? And how can parents help their children eat a balanced diet without turning it into a science or a daily battle at the dinner table? In this roughly 60-minute episode of “Flutlicht & Flipcharts”, you’ll not only get to know BVB’s nutrition expert better, but also discover why a balanced diet is often simpler than many people think. The latest episode and all other episodes of “Flutlicht & Flipcharts”, the podcast that introduces a Borussia Dortmund staff member each month, are available on bvb.de and all major podcast platforms. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: what to watch vs Central Connecticut
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange forward Sadiq White Jr. (1) defends New Haven Chargers forward Teshaun Steele (14) during the second half at the JMA Wireless Dome. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Syracuse Orange (1-0) men’s basketball is back in action tonight when the Central Connecticut Blue Devils (0-1) visit the JMA Dome. Tip-off is 7:00 and streaming on ACCNX. Here’s what our staff is watching for: Szuba: Defense and rebounding Syracuse came out strong defensively to start the season but the intensity waned as the game went on. So too did the rebounding margin. Central Connecticut is one of the worst offensive teams in the country, so can the Orange put the clamps down and close out stops with rebounds? Sadiq White and Gavin Doty looked good in game one, but look to see if the Orange frontcourt can get some more production from the center position against a more feeble interior with less size. Dom: The point guard spot Of note, Garvey Dual and Ryan Moesch essentially split time at the one in Syracuse’s season-opener. Dual played 23 minutes, while Moesch notched 17. The former had the better statline (7 points, 3/5 shooting, and the usual defense), while the latter did put up 0 points on 0/8 shooting, but lead the team in assists (five) and clearly is going to have the ball plenty coming off the bench. Monitoring where this position goes, how both guys are playing, and if this essentially 50-50 split rotation continues. Sam: How does the back of the rotation play out? I was surprised that Amarri Monroe only played nine minutes against New Haven on Monday. I was also surprised that Francis Folefac didn’t check into the game at all. I’d like to see GMac go to those guys – and Tasman Goodrick – a little bit more in order to have them feel out the game leading into the games where you’ll need to lean heavier on the top of the rotation next week. Max: Defense James already mentioned it, but after a great and intense defensive start the Orange started to fade out in their defense. I’d like to see them keep up that level they were at and force turnovers when possible. Syracuse should also look to establish themselves as the dominant force throughout this game so they can translate defense to scoring. Kevin: Push the Pace Look we all anticipate that this squad is going to try and rely on their defense, but on Monday the Orange scored four fast-break points. That’s just two baskets on the break despite getting 9 steals and 6 blocks. For a team with an unproven half-court offense, they need to get some easy points. I’m going to be a broken record this season, but if you build a roster around positional length you need to generate some easy baskets. ********************************************************************************************* What will you be watching for in this one?

item.title: Newcastle’s Aladji Bamba January Exit Update Emerges Amid Lack of Playing Time
item.description: COVENTRY, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 12: Aladji Bamba of Newcastle United looks on during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Coventry City and Newcastle United at The Coventry Building Society Arena on October 12, 2026 in Coventry, England. (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images) Aladji Bamba’s first months at Newcastle United have seen him get far fewer opportunities than expected, with the £30 million summer signing playing only 27 minutes of Premier League football so far. On Tuesday, The Athletic’s Chris Waugh reported that loaning him out in January is something Newcastle should consider if the 20-year-old remains unable to earn meaningful minutes under Matthias Jaissle. “If Bamba cannot get any game time in the Carabao Cup, then it would make sense for him to get minutes out on loan,” Waugh wrote. Jaissle admitted before the game against Everton that Bamba has found the physical adjustment to Premier League football more difficult than initially expected, although the head coach believes the midfielder is beginning to adapt to the British game. On top of that, Newcastle’s hierarchy is reportedly not making any immediate judgments on Bamba and still expects his role could grow as the season progresses. However, Waugh noted that sporting director Ross Wilson and Jaissle will need to make a collective call before January. “It does feel like Newcastle have too many midfielders to try to fit into this 4-2-3-1 system, and Bamba is currently the obvious candidate to send out on loan,” Waugh wrote. Should Newcastle loan Bamba out in January, or keep him around and continue his development within Jaissle’s squad? Share your thoughts in the comments. Join the conversation! item.title: U.S.-Sanctioned Moscow Exchange Will List Bitcoin on Dec. 1 as Russia Pulls Crypto Trading Home
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S.-Sanctioned Moscow Exchange Will List Bitcoin on Dec. 1 as Russia Pulls Crypto Trading Home Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, will begin trading bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT on Dec. 1, the exchange announced this week, calling it the country’s first organized market for digital currencies. The launch puts bitcoin on the same screens Russians use to trade Sberbank and Gazprom shares. It also puts a major crypto venue inside an institution that sits under U.S. sanctions. The first phase will run as a pilot. Participants will connect as they are ready, and the exchange said interest has come from existing members, their clients and businesses that already use digital currencies for investment and settlement. How the Moscow market will work Trading will run on the exchange’s existing stock market technology and follow its stock market hours, from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, the exchange told Russian newspaper Vedomosti. The National Clearing Centre, the exchange’s clearing arm, will clear every trade. From day one, clients can settle trades the same day or the next day, and the exchange will offer swaps to help participants manage liquidity. BTC, ETH and USDT will trade in both addressed and addressless modes, and the list is set to grow over time with Russian and international instruments. Custody will run through partner digital depositaries, a new type of entity created under the country’s rules. A Moscow Exchange executive first previewed the plan on Oct. 31. Retail access is tight. Non-qualified investors must pass a test before they can buy, and they can purchase no more than 300,000 rubles of digital currency a year, roughly $3,700, through a single broker. Qualified investors face no cap. The exchange had first flagged plans to debut bitcoin trading in October. For the exchange, the structure keeps crypto inside a regime it already runs. Brokers connect the way they do for equities, trades net through the same clearing system and investor classifications carry over from the stock market. That lowers the barrier for banks and brokerages that want to offer bitcoin without building separate custody and matching systems of their own. Sanctions loom over USDT The U.S. Treasury blocked Moscow Exchange and the National Clearing Centre in June 2024 as part of a broader push against Russia’s financial system over the war in Ukraine. That makes the clearing house holding customers’ USDT a sanctioned entity. Tether routinely freezes wallets tied to addresses on the Treasury’s sanctions list, which raises questions about how the stablecoin issuer would treat USDT held through the Moscow clearing structure. Neither the exchange nor Tether has publicly addressed that issue. The choice of USDT, a dollar-pegged token, is notable for a market built in part to operate outside the dollar system. Bitcoin and ether carry no issuer that can freeze balances. Pulling offshore activity home The market rests on Federal

item.title: Putin slams ‘political’ moves to keep Russia out of sport events
item.description: Vladimir Putin on Thursday slammed countries who oppose reinstating Russia into international sports as several European teams said they will refuse to play them at next year’s world ice hockey championships over the Ukraine war. Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Czech Republic on Tuesday all followed Finland in saying they would not play Russia at the 2027 world championships to be held in Germany. Russia has been banned from International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) events since Putin launched the 2022 war in Ukraine, but the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of admitting them to the world championships. Russia has been mostly banned from international sport since 2022 but some restrictions have eased in recent months — a trend slammed by Ukraine. Putin praised the International Olympic Committee and CAS for “taking decisions to uphold the Olympic Charter and its principles”, as restrictions have been eased. “Unfortunately, however, not all countries are prepared to honour the commitments they once undertook, and restrictions on Russian sport — which are political rather than legal — continue,” Putin told a televised government meeting. Amid the ice hockey stand-off, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday Russia would not be allowed to compete at next month’s World Junior Hockey Championships. The world championships are due to be held in Germany next May, but the draw and scheduling for the tournament have already taken place, without Russia. Putin has regularly appeared playing ice hockey during his long presidency. Russia’s war against Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, forced millions to displace and is Europe’s worst conflict since World War II. item.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout Wipes Out Leveraged Longs
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes Over 5% to $75,000 as Tech Rout Wipes Out Leveraged Longs Bitcoin price fell about 5% on Thursday morning, sliding from above $80,800 to near $76,000 as a sharp selloff in technology stocks spread into crypto and wiped out leveraged traders betting on further gains, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The drop erased the rebound that had carried bitcoin back above $80,000 overnight. It touched a low near $76,100 shortly after the U.S. stock market opened, its weakest level since the start of the week. The reversal came fast. Bitcoin held near $80,000 through Wednesday, and early Thursday traders were cheering a short squeeze that pushed it past $80,500. Within roughly two hours of the opening bell, the bitcoin price was more than $4,000 lower. Wall Street’s AI trade breaks The trigger sat on Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled as much as 3.9% on Thursday and slipped into correction territory, trading 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 fell about 2%, erasing Wednesday’s rally, its best session in three months. Chip and AI stocks took the worst of it. Nvidia and Broadcom each fell about 5%, Tesla lost around 9% and neocloud names CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN dropped between 9% and 13%. Qualcomm slid 9% after a weak outlook. Sandisk was down nearly 19% at the time of writing. Investors are pricing in a Democratic-controlled Congress after Tuesday’s midterms. Traders fear new limits on the data center buildout, and UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of U.S. data center capacity additions expected in 2028 could be at risk from construction pauses, Reuters reported. The selling started in Asia, where South Korea’s Kospi closed down more than 5% as Samsung and SK hynix sank. U.S. stocks shed $2.3 trillion in market value within the first hour of trading, with the Russell 2000 plunging 2.5% and on pace for its biggest one-day drop since June 5 Bitcoin price has traded alongside that AI-heavy tech complex for most of the year, and bitcoin miners are now part of it. Many have sold bitcoin to fund AI data centers, so the same political risk now weighs on both. Leverage unwinds Leverage turned the move into a flush. Roughly $370 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in about an hour as bitcoin broke $77,000 and ether fell below $2,300, most of them long bets. Wider tallies circulating on X put long liquidations closer to $400 million over the same 60 minutes. The U.S. stock market shed more than $1 trillion in value within minutes of the open, and crypto went with it. Wednesday’s short squeeze had pulled in late buyers with borrowed money. When stocks broke, those positions were the first to go, and forced selling pushed the bitcoin price through support around $77,000. item.title: Ukraine Central Bank Refuses to Back Crypto Bill Cleared for Second Reading
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Ukraine Central Bank Refuses to Back Crypto Bill Cleared for Second Reading Ukraine’s central bank will not support a crypto market bill that a parliamentary committee cleared for a final vote, warning that the draft leaves foreign tokens that act like electronic money outside its control and risks monetary sovereignty. The National Bank of Ukraine said in a Nov. 4 statement that Draft Law No. 10225-d on the circulation of virtual assets, recommended by the Verkhovna Rada Committee on Finance, Tax and Customs Policy for adoption in the second reading and as a whole, fails to reflect compromises struck during drafting. The NBU said it received the final text only late the evening before the committee vote and that the process “was not sufficiently transparent.” Deputy Governor Oleksii Shaban raised the bank’s objections at the committee meeting, but the NBU said the format did not allow a full debate. Ukraine already legalized a framework for virtual assets in 2022. The new bill is meant to put that market under detailed rules modeled on the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, or MiCA, and on International Monetary Fund recommendations. The NBU says it supports that direction in principle. Three risks the NBU flags The bank’s public case rests on three points. First, the draft would let foreign tokens into Ukraine even when they function as electronic money but face no matching supervision in the countries where they are issued. That, the NBU said, threatens monetary sovereignty, the transmission of monetary policy, payment infrastructure and financial stability. The bank wants the same power it has over domestically issued tokens: the authority to assess those foreign assets and, when needed, restrict their circulation in Ukraine. Second, simplified admission of foreign virtual assets must not let them sidestep rules that apply to comparable Ukrainian assets. Without that parity, the NBU warned, segments of the market could expand outside adequate oversight and create regulatory arbitrage. Third, the bank flagged monopolization and corruption risks in how the National Securities and Stock Market Commission would authorize trading-platform operators. The NBU initially opposed numerical caps, then agreed as a compromise to limit the first wave to three legal persons chosen by competitive selection. The final draft, it said, drops a clear five-year cap and leaves the number of operators to the securities commission’s discretion without enough antitrust safeguards. What the bill would do next The committee’s Nov. 4 recommendation does not enact the law. A final Verkhovna Rada vote is expected later in November. If adopted, the rules would take effect on July 1, 2027, Interfax Ukraine reported , splitting supervision between the NBU and the securities commission. item.title: 2027: Police assure corps members, ad hoc staff of protection
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has assured members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and other ad hoc staff to be engaged by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of adequate protection during the 2027 general elections. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, gave the assurance at a joint media briefing of the Forum of Security and Intelligence Agencies, organised by the Office of the National Security Adviser. He was responding to concerns over reported abductions of corps members in different parts of the country, particularly as they are expected to form a significant part of INEC’s ad hoc workforce during the elections. Iniedu said the police had conducted an extensive threat assessment and were strengthening security arrangements to protect electoral personnel and materials and ensure the smooth conduct of the polls. He said the arrangements would be implemented in collaboration with other security agencies before, during and after the elections. “In every election cycle, there are potential threats to soft targets. However, as other targets become increasingly fortified by security agencies, criminals may attempt to exploit perceived vulnerabilities elsewhere. “The Nigeria Police Force has conducted an extensive threat assessment ahead of the forthcoming general elections, and we are adequately preparing for the challenges. “During the Osun State election, for instance, we engaged corps members, their parents and other stakeholders and assured them of our commitment to providing adequate security for all ad hoc personnel. We came out unscathed. The forthcoming general election will not be an exception,” he said. The police spokesman said the force was working with sister security agencies and engaging INEC to strengthen protection for corps members and other personnel involved in the electoral process. He added that deployments were being increased, while the Inspector-General of Police had directed the immediate distribution of operational equipment and logistics. Emphasising that the safety of corps members and other young Nigerians participating in the electoral process remained a priority, Iniedu said the police would do everything within their capacity to protect them. He also warned political actors against hate speech, incitement and other forms of political violence capable of undermining the electoral process. item.title: Shettima rally: SDP denies sponsoring disruption, faults Nasarawa govt
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State has denied allegations linking its governorship candidate, retired Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, and former Governor Tanko Al-Makura to the disruption of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Lafia. The party also accused the Nasarawa State Government of attempting to find scapegoats among opposition figures following the incident at Lafia Square on Wednesday, where President Bola Tinubu was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima. Reacting to the allegation in a statement on Thursday, Deputy Director-General, Media, Publicity and Communication, and spokesperson for the SDP governorship campaign council, Makpa Malla, described a statement by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Shuaibu Magaji Labaran, as reckless, irresponsible and politically motivated. Malla particularly faulted the government’s reference to Al-Makura and Adamu as suspected sponsors of the disruption, describing it as a serious allegation of criminal complicity and conspiracy. “The most disturbing aspect of the government’s statement is paragraph three, which expressly names H.E. Senator Umaru Tanko Al-Makura and rtd. IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, the Governorship Candidate of the SDP, as suspected sponsors of the alleged disruption,” the statement said. The campaign council argued that publicly linking the individuals to an alleged criminal act without presenting verifiable evidence raised questions about defamation, due process and the alleged abuse of governmental authority. It maintained that the use of the expression “suspected to be sponsored” did not absolve the government of responsibility for making damaging allegations against identifiable individuals. The SDP said if the government had credible intelligence implicating the individuals, it should submit such evidence to the appropriate investigative authorities rather than make public accusations. It cautioned against what it described as a trial by press release, insisting that political opponents should not be pronounced guilty in the court of public opinion. The party also criticised the state government over what it described as more pressing governance challenges, including political grievances arising from the APC’s internal primaries, which it claimed contributed to tensions surrounding the incident. The SDP, however, said it would welcome the outcome of an independent, evidence-based investigation into the disruption, provided it was free from political interference. It specifically called for the Department of State Services (DSS), which is expected to investigate the incident, to be allowed to discharge its responsibilities professionally without pressure to validate predetermined allegations. “The DSS must be allowed to do its work professionally, without being turned into an instrument for settling political scores or intimidating perceived political opponents,” the

item.title: Uzodinma’s senatorial bid: Wike denies involvement in court ruling
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has denied involvement in the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the recognition of Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo-West senatorial district in the 2027 general elections. Wike made the denial during his ongoing media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on Thursday, describing allegations linking him to the judgment as mischievous. The minister, however, acknowledged his disagreement with Uzodinma over the Rainbow Coalition, a political structure supporting President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. “I didn’t go to court; I’m not from APC. People are saying that because a day before that judgment he had openly warned his people there’s no Rainbow Coalition; if I see you I’ll collect the vehicle. So when the judgment came, they said it was me. How could it have been me?” Wike said. He challenged the Imo governor to explain his opposition to the coalition, asking, “What is Hope Uzodinma afraid of in the Rainbow Coalition?” Wike maintained that the coalition’s primary objective was to secure victory for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, while other considerations, including zoning, would determine outcomes at the National Assembly level. He also defended his political relationship with former Imo governor, Rochas Okorocha, despite their political differences, saying he would not harm his friends because of their associations with political opponents. On the 2027 presidential race, Wike dismissed the chances of former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, who is the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress. The minister criticised Amaechi’s record in office, citing alleged shortcomings in projects and expenditure during his tenure. “It’ll be difficult no matter how you look at it,” Wike said of Amaechi’s candidacy, adding, “His candidacy is dead on arrival.” Wike also defended his political arrangements involving candidates across the APC and PDP, saying he had conceded 13 seats to the APC and three to the PDP. He said the decisions were reached through consultations over the past two years, adding that his supporters had been briefed on their roles. “Leadership is about cascading impact down to your people,” he said. item.title: Two kidnapped visually impaired persons regain freedom in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Two visually impaired persons abducted by gunmen along Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State have regained their freedom. The victims were kidnapped on Monday night while returning to Jos from Benue State, where they had attended a training programme. Chairman of the Plateau State chapter of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD), Shindol Aaron, confirmed their release in a telephone interview, saying they regained their freedom on Wednesday night. He said, “We were lucky yesterday that they released them. I spoke with the brothers who went to pick them up, and they confirmed that the victims were already in a vehicle coming into town.” Aaron said the victims were released between 9pm and 10pm after spending time in the custody of their abductors. On reports that the abductors had been arrested, he said, “Information reached me that the culprits had been apprehended by security men, but I have not verified that information.” “I was called and informed that they had been apprehended, although I am yet to independently confirm it.” The JONAPWD chairman said he had not personally met with the victims since their release, adding that he was yet to establish direct contact with them. The victims were among nine persons travelling in a vehicle to attend a training programme in Benue State when gunmen attacked them along Riyom on Monday night. Seven other occupants of the vehicle reportedly escaped during the attack. The abductors had demanded N50 million ransom for the release of the two visually impaired persons. The post Two kidnapped visually impaired persons regain freedom in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fed and OCC Quiz U.S. Banks After $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Fed and OCC Quiz U.S. Banks After $6.3 Billion Binance Hack U.S. bank regulators contacted banks this week to check whether their systems had any vulnerabilities after last week’s $6.3 billion hack of Binance, Reuters reported Thursday, citing several people familiar with the matter. Supervisors from the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency began reaching out to banks on Monday morning, asking about any unusual activity or disruption in their services. The outreach shows regulators are treating the largest crypto theft on record as a possible risk to traditional finance, not just a problem for crypto exchanges, at a time when links between banks and the crypto industry have tightened. Banks run diagnostics One source at a bank that regulators contacted told Reuters there had been no disruptions to its services. Employees there prepared talking points for customers but have since received few inquiries. Banks have been studying the attack and running diagnostics on their own systems to make sure they could defend against something similar, two people familiar with the efforts said. Within hours of the hack, a cybersecurity team at one of the largest U.S. banks reached out to counterparts at Binance. That team is writing an internal report that will lead to a review of the bank’s systems and possibly cybersecurity updates. It was not yet clear whether the bank would be vulnerable to the same tactics. The biggest concern, one person said, is that artificial intelligence models have been evolving quickly, making it hard for banks to keep up with hackers. Banks are devoting a lot of resources to reviewing and patching their cybersecurity code. Binance said it was not aware of conversations between banks and regulators or whether the hack had any impact on U.S. banks. “We are in close contact with regulators all over the world, keeping them up to date on this security breach,” a Binance spokesperson said. How the Binance hack worked The concern about AI tracks with how the attack unfolded. Binance said the theft began with a fake job interview and ran for five months before any coins moved. The campaign combined a poisoned software download, a staged recruitment process, malware that evaded endpoint detection and an internal AI tool that the attackers turned against the company’s own wallet engineers. Funds began leaving Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. Blockchain analysis firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs linked the hack to TraderTraitor, a unit associated with North Korea. Binance reopened withdrawals in stages four days later, starting with bitcoin. It has said it froze or intercepted about $2.85 billion of the stolen assets and replenished 98% of affected tokens from its own funds. None of the techniques Binance described are unique to crypto. item.title: FG blames gas shortages, maintenance for power outages in five states
item.description: By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor The Federal Government has attributed electricity supply disruptions in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo States to inadequate gas supply, reduced hydroelectric generation and maintenance challenges. The Federal Ministry of Power, in a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, assured Nigerians that efforts were underway to restore normal electricity supply in the affected areas. The Ministry acknowledged the impact of the outages on households, businesses and public institutions, particularly in areas that had recently recorded improvements in electricity supply. It stated: “We recognise what every hour without power means for individuals, families and businesses, and we do not take it lightly.” Explaining the causes of the disruptions, the Ministry said preliminary assessments showed that they were not caused by any major or systemic failure of the national grid. According to the statement, “They stem from maintenance and operational issues on parts of the power ecosystem, together with a decline in generation caused by constraints in gas supply to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower water inflows into reservoirs.” It added that the challenges were being addressed by relevant operators. The Ministry disclosed that the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, was working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) and Electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) to accelerate restoration. It said Tegbe had engaged the operators to resolve the operational constraints, fast-track ongoing maintenance and provide regular updates to consumers. Reaffirming the government’s commitment to improving electricity supply, the Ministry stated: “Nigerians deserve better power, and this administration is working to deliver it.” The Minister thanked consumers for their patience and understanding, promising further updates as restoration progresses. The statement was signed by Adeola Adelabu, Special Adviser (Media and Publicity) to the Minister. item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe bounces back from communications glitch in interstellar space
item.description: null Voyager, 1, humanity's most distant spacecraft, is back in contact after briefly losing touch with Earth last month. The spacecraft stopped phoning home for about 48 hours between Oct. 18 and 20 due to a communications glitch that Voyager 1 resolved on its own, before engineers could send the long-running spacecraft a remote fix. "This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said in an agency statement about the incident on Oct. 29. Voyager 1 is almost one light-day from Earth, meaning that a command takes nearly a day to reach the spacecraft and a response takes another day to come back to our planet. The spacecraft will reach the light-day milestone on Nov. 18, at 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth. NASA's Deep Space Network of three antennas does check-ins to make sure the spacecraft is doing well. On Oct. 18 and 19, Voyager 1 did not respond. Its signal fortunately reappeared on Oct. 20. "Engineers still are investigating what caused the communication loss," JPL added in the statement, but said it appears Voyager 1 went into a sort of safe mode. "The team has so far determined that one group of thrusters went offline and their backups turned on. Such a swap is programmed to occur automatically if the spacecraft computers detect something amiss with the active thrusters." Voyager 1 and its still-operational twin, Voyager 2 , both launched in 1977 on an initial mission to explore planets in the solar system. The two spacecraft took advantage of a rare alignment that allowed them to swing from Jupiter to Saturn to Uranus and Neptune using a minimum of fuel, although funding to explore the more distant planets and moons was not guaranteed at launch. The spacecraft duly swung by Jupiter's and Saturn's systems (some months apart from each other) to great acclaim before parting pathways. Voyager 1's close-up view of Saturn's rings as well as the moon Titan — which may have prebiotic or pre-life chemistry — altered the spacecraft's trajectory to put it high above the plane of the solar system. Meanwhile, Voyager 2 flew on to Uranus and Neptune in 1986 and 1989, respectively, providing the only up-close view of these planetary systems to date. An image of Saturn taken by Voyager 1 on Nov. 16, 1980, four days after the spacecraft flew past the planet. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Running on nuclear power, and continuing to deliver valuable science from deep space, the Voyagers saw their missions extended repeatedly. Both crossed into interstellar space a few years ago, and are still operational. But with age comes a cost: the plutonium power sources on both spacecraft are diminishing, requiring engineers to periodically shut off instruments or come up with other clever ways of saving power. item.title: Court admits FG’s evidence against six alleged coup plotters
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday admitted in evidence exhibits tendered by the Federal Government against six persons accused of complicity in an alleged plot to overthrow President Bola Tinubu’s administration through a coup d’état. Among the proof of evidence the court admitted were extrajudicial statements the defendants made before a Special Investigation Panel and military police authorities. Those on trial over the alleged coup are retired Major General Mohammed Ibrahim Gana; retired Naval Captain Erasmus Ochegobia Victor; a serving Police Inspector, Ahmed Ibrahim; and three others: Zekeri Umoru, Bukar Kashim Goni and Abdulkadir Sani. They are answering to a 13-count charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/206/2026. The defendants had challenged the admissibility of their statements on the premise that they were not made voluntarily but through coercion, in violation of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. The defence lawyers further contended that their clients were denied the right to legal representation during interrogation, insisting there were discrepancies between the video recordings and the defendants’ written statements. Although the prosecution urged the court to dismiss the objections, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik ordered a trial within a trial to ascertain the voluntariness of the extrajudicial statements sought to be tendered. The issue arose while the fourth prosecution witness was testifying. Delivering the ruling on Thursday, Justice Abdulmalik held that the defendants failed to establish their allegation that they were coerced into making confessional statements. The court described the defendants’ claim that they spoke under duress as an afterthought, and it dismissed their allegation of torture. It went ahead to admit both the defendants’ written statements and the video recordings as part of the proof of evidence in the matter. Justice Abdulmalik fixed December 7 and 10 for the continuation of the hearing on the charge. It will be recalled that one of the defendants, Umoru, revealed on May 20 that discussions were held on how the electricity supply to the Presidential Villa, Abuja, would be switched off to aid the alleged coup. Umoru, an employee of Julius Berger Nigeria Plc in the Maintenance Department at the Presidential Villa, made the disclosure in a video recording played in open court. The defendant said he warned that such an action would immediately trigger investigations and the detention of workers on duty. He alleged that the coup’s purported mastermind, Col. Mohammed Ma’aji, offered him money, through the third defendant, Insp. Ibrahim, to recruit between 18 and 19 persons working inside the villa. Umoru said those to be recruited included soldiers, officials of the Department of State Services (DSS) and Julius Berger staff members. item.title: Memory makers mint megabucks while buyers beg for mercy
item.description: The big memory manufacturers continue to print money at the expense of long-suffering buyers, with industry DRAM revenue approaching five times its level a year ago. Demand for datacenter capacity and AI accelerators drove the 369 percent year-over-year surge in Q3 2026, Counterpoint Research reports . "Bit shipments rose only about 4 percent this quarter, yet DRAM revenue reached nearly $200 billion, close to 5x a year ago," says Counterpoint senior analyst Jeongku Choi. "AI has turned memory from a commodity into a valuable scarce resource, and buyers are now competing for supply rather than negotiating on price. With prices still rising, suppliers are on track to set new earnings records again next quarter." As Reg readers will be well aware by now, the AI infrastructure boom has sent demand for server memory soaring. Manufacturers have prioritized more lucrative products for that market, squeezing supplies for PCs, smartphones, and other devices. The consequences have been a sharp increase in memory costs, leading to higher prices of products that use it. The average price tag for a laptop or desktop was up by double-digit percentages across Europe this summer, resulting in falling PC shipments as vendors struggled to secure supplies and buyers were put off by the expense. A similar effect has been seen in the smartphone arena, with shipments down by at least a fifth as rising memory costs squeezed budget models out of the market, leaving vendors to focus on high-end devices instead. Price increases slowed from the steep rises seen in the first half of the year, Counterpoint says, but average DRAM selling prices still reached $1.90 per gigabit and remained the main driver of revenue growth. Of the big three memory makers – the DRAMvirate, if you like – Samsung led with a 38 percent share of DRAM revenue. Separately, it forecast company-wide operating profit of about $80 billion for Q3, up from $9 billion a year earlier. SK hynix posted stronger sequential growth, helping it recover some of the share it lost earlier this year, according to Counterpoint. The firm made a $62.8 billion profit , and predicts that memory shortages will persist until at least 2030. Micron's DRAM revenue grew more slowly than rivals', but its wider business hardly suffered: fiscal fourth-quarter net profit reached $37.7 billion , exceeding its entire second-quarter revenue of $23.8 billion. Counterpoint's research director MS Hwang expects to see memory prices remaining high next year. "[High-bandwidth memory] prices, which lagged commodity DRAM this year, are now catching up. Long-term agreements (LTAs) are supporting prices, and supply will stay tight because major new fabs will not start production until 2028. LTA terms may cause results to differ between suppliers in the short term, but over time they should all follow the same upward trend," he says. That means more bad news for buyers, but more massive profits for the memory makers. ®

item.title: 2027: Ajimobi, Folarin, Adelabu lead Oyo APC reconciliation push
item.description: By Adeola Badru Efforts to resolve internal divisions and strengthen the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections have gained momentum following a meeting involving prominent party leaders. The meeting, led by former Oyo State First Lady and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Austria, Mrs Florence Ajimobi, brought together the Oyo State Coordinator of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Teslim Kolawole Folarin; Senator Abdulfatai Buhari, representing Oyo North Senatorial District; former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu; and Barrister Akeem Agbaje. The meeting focused on resolving internal disagreements, promoting inclusive leadership and rebuilding unity within the party ahead of the 2027 elections. According to sources familiar with the discussions, participants emphasised the need to set aside personal differences and competing interests in the collective interest of the party. They reportedly agreed that greater cohesion among party leaders and stakeholders would strengthen the APC’s political structure and improve its chances in the state. The discussions also highlighted the importance of sustained consultations among critical stakeholders and ensuring that different tendencies within the party were accommodated in its decision-making process. A major issue raised at the meeting was the need to translate calls for reconciliation into concrete actions aimed at rebuilding trust, addressing grievances and encouraging cooperation among party leaders and members. With the 2027 elections approaching, the engagement was seen as part of renewed efforts by influential party figures to harmonise interests and prevent lingering disagreements from affecting the APC’s preparations. The participants also underscored the importance of developing a collective political strategy capable of carrying all stakeholders along and strengthening the party’s electoral prospects across Oyo State. item.title: Earth photobombs spacewalking Canadian astronaut | Space photo of the day for Nov. 5, 2026
item.description: null Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk poses for a photo during his spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: CSA) Spacewalks are hard work, so sometimes you need to take a break for a moment and snap a gorgeous selfie with your home planet in the background. What is it? During a pre-Halloween spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk took a moment to pose for a photograph. In this moment , the International Space Station to which he was tethered was orbiting 267 miles (430 kilometers) above the South Atlantic Ocean down below on Earth. During this spacewalk — the first for a Canadian since 2019 — Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon worked together to install a new roll-out solar array on the station while also performing some "get ahead" tasks to prep for the next spacewalk, which is happening today (Nov. 5). During today's excursion, the same two astronauts will venture out into space, tethered to the space station, to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array. These eight new arrays will boost the station's available power by a total of 30%, according to NASA officials. Why is it incredible? When we think of astronauts working in space, we might think of the important science and research they're doing aboard the station. Astronauts work on everything from biomedical research to plant science and physics experiments. But the job also includes work on the space station itself. Sometimes they have to venture out into the vacuum of space to fix urgent problems. These situations can be tense, and there's a lot of pressure to get things absolutely right. But even spacewalks that do relatively mundane maintenance work, like the one on Oct. 29, come with pressure. Every minute that astronauts spend outside of the space station, there are countless risk factors floating around. Earth orbit is a very harsh environment, after all, even if it does allow for some pretty amazing selfies.

item.title: The hidden supply chain costs of the AI boom
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Willy Shih, an economist, a professor of management practice at Harvard Business School, and the author of the upcoming book, Where Does My Stuff Come From? The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains . Willy is one of my all-time favorite Decoder guests — his way of looking at the world through our supply chains is just a fascinating way of making sense of the global economy. I first met Willy in 2019, while The Verge was covering Foxconn’s promise to build an LCD fab in Wisconsin. That obviously never happened, but Willy called it right away because he could see the supply chain to support a fab simply wasn’t in place. We also had Willy on the show in 2021 to talk about what was then the pandemic-era chip shortage. Now, five years later, we’re in another manufacturing mess, as we stand in the middle of a political fight over whether globalization is coming to an end. Trumps’ tariffs keep changing, the factories that were supposed to reshore in America mostly haven’t materialized, and AI is devouring the planet’s computing resources during an unprecedented infrastructure buildout. Willy’s new book is all about the economics underlying these complex systems, which our politicians and regulators seem to insistently ignore. You’ll hear us talk about why the markets have reacted to all these disruptions the way they have, and why China remains a global manufacturing powerhouse even though every other country thinks that’s so risky. I loved this conversation — it’s in the weeds, and Willy really knows his stuff. Okay: economist Will Shih on his new book Where Does My Stuff Come From? Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Willy Shih, you’re an economist and professor of management practice at Harvard. You’re also the author of the new book, Where Does My Stuff Come From: The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains . Welcome back to Decoder . Well, thanks for having me back. I am very excited to talk to you. You and I first started talking ages ago when The Verge was covering Foxconn in Wisconsin. You are a reliable source of information on what it takes to actually build an LCD plant anywhere, not just in Wisconsin. The Foxconn in Wisconsin thing was funny because I tend to go on first principles on these things. Once I knew they weren’t going to build a glass plant across the street, it’s like there’s no way there’s going to be a factory. Now, what happened afterwards, of course, is people heard your show, and then I started getting calls from people who live in the community. They went to the zoning hearings in town, then sent me the plans and asked, “Is this going to be a panel factory?” I said, “No, I told you it’s not going to be a panel factory.” So they sent me the plans. I said, “Well, there’s not enough concrete to make this a panel factory.” For a panel factory, you need stability, so you gotta have all this structural steel, and you have to have all this concrete. item.title: New hoax bomb threats hit European flights
item.description: Italian, French and Bulgarian fighter jets scrambled Thursday as about 20 flights were hit by a third day of hoax bomb alerts across Europe, authorities and airlines said. The hoaxes involved flights from Greece to Britain, but particularly targeted low-cost carriers and flights to or from Bulgaria, Czech Republic and Italy. Three flights were diverted but all the jets landed safely with no explosives found. No claim of responsibility was made for all the flights, but a threat against two flights sent to airports in Rome and published by an Italian newspaper contained misogynistic messages. – Under escort, diversions – At least five flights received an air force escort after receiving bomb threats. Bulgaria’s air force escorted three Ryanair planes headed for Sofia from Madrid, Copenhagen, and London Stansted. All three planes were inspected and no explosives found, an interior ministry spokesperson told AFP. French fighters accompanied an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin that was headed to Rome, diverting it to the Evreux military base 100 kilometers (60 miles) west of Paris. Other jets were also diverted. The Ryanair flight from London-Stansted to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv Airport, east of the capital, while a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw was re-routed to Vienna, the airlines said. – Who and why – Italian newspaper Il Corriere della Sera published the text of a message sent to ADR, the company that manages Rome’s airports. A company source confirmed the report to AFP. “You are all accomplices in a criminal conspiracy, and for this we want to annihilate you. Right now explosive devices have been placed on the following flights: AY1751 Helsinki–Rome and EI402 Dublin–Rome,” read the message, with media noting it was written in “broken Italian”. “We Male State fighters with our actions today will leave a mark in history. Your feminist regime will remember it forever. The explosion will occur in 60 minutes. Today your sky will be red,” read the text. There is a far-right movement in Russia called the Male State, but AFP could not confirm any link to the message. Prague Airport spokeswoman Denisa Hejtmankova told AFP the airport had received threats in emails from anonymous addresses. The EU’s transport commissioner, Apostolos Tzitzikostas, wrote on X that it was “too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked.” But European authorities say there has been rise in hybrid attacks, sometimes linked to Russia or Iran. – Landing safely – Most of the flights targeted Thursday landed without incident at their original destinations. Those included a Lot Polish Airlines flight from Warsaw to Brussels and a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Bucharest. In the Czech Republic, four targeted planes bound for Prague flown by Ryanair, Easy Jet and Sky Express all landed safely. “We perceive the credibility of the threats as low,” said Czech police on X. “Nevertheless, we are not underestimating the situation, and all necessary securi

item.title: NISO blames gas shortages, low water levels for drop in power generation
item.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) has attributed the decline in electricity generation on the national grid to gas supply constraints affecting thermal power plants and reduced water levels at hydroelectric power stations. The operator disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, explaining that the constraints had reduced available generation and affected electricity allocations to Distribution Companies (DisCos). According to NISO, inadequate gas supply has limited the capacity of affected thermal generating plants to operate at their available levels, while reduced water inflows into reservoirs have weakened output from hydroelectric stations. It said the shortfall had affected the volume of electricity allocated to DisCos for distribution to consumers, resulting in shorter hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. NISO noted that the extent of the impact varied across distribution companies, depending on available generation and their respective electricity allocations. The operator acknowledged the difficulties faced by electricity consumers nationwide, expressing appreciation for the concerns raised by members of the public and other stakeholders. It said efforts were ongoing to diversify the energy mix of the national grid to strengthen electricity supply security and reduce exposure to prevailing operational constraints. NISO reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, optimising the dispatch of available electricity generation and ensuring the secure, reliable and efficient operation of the national grid. The post NISO blames gas shortages, low water levels for drop in power generation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Raphinha extends Barcelona deal by two years
item.description: Captain Raphinha has signed a contract extension until 2030, La Liga champions Barcelona said on Thursday. The 29-year-old Brazilian forward, who joined the Catalan giants in 2022, had been contracted until 2028. “A declaration of intent. Our dear captain will continue to lead our project until 2030,” Barca wrote in a statement. Raphinha said in September that he wanted to extend his deal, and maybe even end his career at Barca. He has been in the form of his life this season, scoring 19 goals and contributing three assists in 13 matches in all competitions. The former Leeds United winger took over the captaincy at the start of the season following the departures of Ronald Araujo and Marc-Andre ter Stegen. He has also shifted inside from his usual position on the wing to fill the gap created by strikers Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres leaving the club. He has been Barca’s most potent forward since German Hansi Flick took over in 2024, leading Barca to back-to-back La Liga crowns. The post Raphinha extends Barcelona deal by two years appeared first on Vanguard News .
