item.title: Tinubu gets opposition backing in Ekiti, Oyebanji pledges 90% votes
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela Ado-Ekiti — President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign received a boost in Ekiti State on Thursday as governorship candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in the June 20 election declared support for his second-term bid. The opposition candidates announced their support at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where Governor Biodun Oyebanji also pledged that the state would deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented the President at the rally, said the support of the former opposition candidates, former governors and other political leaders demonstrated the APC’s growing political strength in the state. He urged Ekiti residents to improve on the 201,495 votes recorded by Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, when the APC won in all 16 local government areas of the state. Shettima recalled that Oyebanji secured 85.74 per cent of the votes in the June governorship election, expressing optimism that the APC would increase its performance in the presidential poll. He said the Federal Government had taken difficult decisions to address the country’s economic challenges and that the benefits of the reforms were beginning to emerge. “With a total registered vote of 1,028,000, it is our hope, prayer and aspiration that from January 16, 2027, APC will garner 90 to 95 per cent of the votes cast in Ekiti State,” he said. In his remarks, Oyebanji described the rally as a demonstration of political unity in Ekiti, saying the endorsement by former opposition candidates and political leaders had strengthened the APC ahead of the presidential election. He recalled that Tinubu, during his 2022 campaign, had urged Ekiti residents to vote for both him and Oyebanji, promising federal support for the state if elected. According to the governor, the President has fulfilled that promise through what he described as unprecedented federal support for Ekiti since its creation 30 years ago. Oyebanji said the APC’s 85.7 per cent performance in the June governorship election reflected residents’ satisfaction with his administration and the Federal Government’s interventions. He added that the state was determined to improve on its previous electoral performance and deliver not less than 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu. Also speaking, the Director-General of the campaign, Abdulaziz Yari, urged Ekiti residents to deliver at least 800,000 votes for the President, representing about 90 per cent of the state’s votes. Yari said Tinubu had supported the state through investments in education, road construction, youth development and women’s empowerment, urging residents to reciprocate through their votes. item.title: Can 142m Nigerian youths change 2027 elections narrative?
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu Nigerian youths constitute a significant portion of the country’s population at over 142 million. Also, recently the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, disclosed that over 9.32 million young Nigerians registered in the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise. These numbers has made expectations mount over young Nigerians’ potential influence on the 2027 general elections. Read Also: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy However, despite their numerical strength and growing political awareness, questions remain whether they can translate their numbers into decisive electoral power. While some stakeholders believe Nigerian youths are increasingly politically conscious, determined to challenge the status quo and demand accountability, others argue that voter apathy, declining confidence in the electoral process, political manipulations and weak grassroots structures could undermine their participation. Consequently, the debate has shifted beyond whether Nigerian youths are ready to vote to whether they are sufficiently organised, motivated and confident in the electoral system to shape electoral outcomes and hold political leaders accountable. Against this backdrop, stakeholders who spoke on the readiness of Nigerian youths ahead of the 2027 elections offered divergent perspectives. They highlighted the opportunities, frustrations and challenges confronting the country’s youthful population. Nigerian youths are losing hope in elections – Olanrewaju Jerry Tobi Olanrewaju, is ‘The Chief Farmer of Africa’, and Founder and Team Lead, Jet Farms and Agro Solutions Limited, based in Abuja. He asserted that most Nigerian youths are losing hope in exercising their franchise as eligible voters. Olanrewaju said: “Honestly, I was hopeful. But over time, many young Nigerians, particularly young farmers, have begun to lose hope. Many of the farmers I work with cannot even feel the impact of the government’s Renewed Hope Agenda. While some macroeconomic indicators may suggest progress, the reality on the farms tells a different story. “The rising cost of inputs, high transportation costs, limited access to affordable financing, and unstable markets have made farming increasingly difficult. “Many young people who once saw agriculture as an opportunity are now afraid to farm because they are uncertain about their survival and returns on investment.” In his counsel he said, “As we approach 2027, Nigerian youths must move beyond social media conversations and become intentional about shaping the elections. “However, their participation must be driven by issues, accountability, credible leadership, and policies that address their everyday realities.” Nigerian youths tired of manipulation, ready to change narrative – Donald Abareowei Benaembele Donald is a vibrant youth leader in Bayelsa State and also the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Gologolo Global Views Enterprise. item.title: France Workers Strike, March For ‘Dignified Wage’
item.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. More than 250,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon, the major labour union CGT said. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesters take part in a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Bordeaux on November 5, 2026. Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. “We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage,” he said. As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument’s website. School blockades Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country’s 3,700 high schools. A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 such secondary schools, including those blockaded and those closed on a day of strikes. Around 16 percent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school, an AFP reporter said. French police officers march amid the smoke during a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks, in Nantes on November 5, 2026. item.title: Tinubu: APC targets 800,000 votes in Ekiti, says North will deliver
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Tinubu The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has set a target of 800,000 votes in Ekiti State for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, with the Director General of its Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, assuring that Northern Nigeria “is ready for Asiwaju 2027” and “is going to deliver him from A to Z.” Yari spoke on Thursday at the party’s campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where he asked the state to improve on the roughly 80 per cent it gave Tinubu in 2022. “Out of 1,080,000 votes, and PVC collected over 900,000, this is my request, and by extension, of course, of the President to you. We are looking for 800,000 votes, representing about 90 per cent,” he said. He told the gathering that the state governor had earlier given a breakdown of the Tinubu administration’s achievements and said the president “did not forget Ekiti”, citing schools, universities, roads, education support for youths and women empowerment. Yari said the candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP, the Allied Peoples Movement APM and the Social Democratic Party SDP who contested the last governorship election against the governor were at the rally “to show solidarity, their togetherness with the Governor when it comes to Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027.” He added that the reward for a heavy turnout would be more federal presence in the state. “The President promised to do more for the Ekiti people,” he said. Turning to the North, Yari said, “We in Northern Nigeria, Bola, are more of us than you in Ekiti, than you in Ondo, than you in Oyo, than you in Osun, than you in Lagos. Bola Ahmed supported our children and supported our people to become number one citizens in this country up to three times. So, we in the north, we are ready for Asiwaju 2027, and we are going to deliver him from A to Z.” The PCC boss also challenged the opposition to say what it would do differently. “What are they going to do differently than what we are having today? Government brings down the inflation,” he said. “As we promised Nigerians, we are going to campaign with our numbers, with what we have done for Nigerians. We are not AI product people. We are saying the truth, and we are asking to go and take that truth. “All the numbers are there, ranging from inflation, ranging from exchange rates, and ranging from balance of trade. All of them are there for anyone to go and take. If they have answers, we are waiting for their answers,” he added. The National Chairman of the APC, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, said his role at the rally was to present the party’s candidates, “starting from the President down to the National Assembly to the House of Assembly candidates in Ekiti state.” Yilwatda pointed to road projects in the state, some of them ongoing and some completed by the president. “We have a road from here to Akure constructed by Mr President. The FCT Minister spoke on Wednesday during his monthly ministerial press briefing in Port Harcourt on Thursday. Wike said he enjoyed his job as FCT Minister and remained committed to it. “I enjoy my job as FCT Minister, and I’m committed to it. Yes, I have pressure to deliver, but positively,” he said. Wike also said Ogoni people had benefited from empowerment under the President. “Ogoni people have been looking for empowerment, and now President Tinubu has done a lot of empowerment for them. He sold out gas turbine, so what’s the impact of his leadership on Rivers people?” Wike further alleged that Amaechi contracted a Ghanaian to plant trees along Aba Road for N8bn. “My brother, it was terrible! item.title: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins is the 1st Black woman to command a space mission. Will we see more diversity in the future on the final frontier?
item.description: null When Jessica Watkins became commander of her mission to the International Space Station, she didn't just fulfill her duty as an astronaut — she made history. Watkins is commanding SpaceX's Crew-13 mission , which launched her and three other astronauts to the I nternational Space Station on Oct. 1. As their Crew Dragon capsule lifted off atop a Falcon 9 rocket that day, Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crewed mission to space. Spaceflight and space science are historically white and male-dominated fields, so this milestone carries incredible significance. "This is certainly an important milestone, I think both for our agency and for the country," Watkins said in a press briefing ahead of Crew-13's launch. This is Watkins' second spaceflight. She previously flew on SpaceX's Crew-4 mission in 2022 and has spent more than 200 days in space to date, though that number will keep climbing for a while, as Crew-13 is set to be an approximately six-month mission. A geologist, astronaut, aquanaut and former professional rugby player, Watkins brings an incredible variety of skills to her new role as mission commander. And, in addition to what she's bringing to her colleagues on mission, she's also providing some serious inspiration for those back on Earth. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins floats in the International Space Station’s cupola during the Crew-4 mission in this photo, which NASA shared on May 9, 2022. (Image credit: NASA) "Jessica is an inspirational symbol to a lot of people," commercial astronaut and fellow geologist Sian Proctor , who became the first Black woman to pilot a spacecraft on SpaceX's private Inspiration4 mission to orbit in September 2021, told Space.com . Sian shared that the two even crossed paths years ago, when their astronaut training aligned. "It just means so much to so many people when you see a diverse crew, and particularly women, and women of color, in leadership positions," Proctor said. "And it means something for America." The visibility of Watkins' accomplishments and missions carries significant cultural weight. However, in addition to recognizing her many achievements, "you also should celebrate the fact that she's African American and a role model for her community," Proctor said. Sian Proctor from aboard the SpaceX Dragon capsule during the Inspiration4 mission. item.title: Microsoft fixed Excel 2016 copy-paste bug. Then reintroduced it. Now it's fixed again
item.description: The Excel copy-and-paste bug is back, which means Microsoft is making a second round of fixes. The bug first appeared in the September update and manifested in multiple versions of Excel as a silent failure of the paste operation. Users copied content and attempted to paste it, but the destination cell was unchanged no matter how hard they mashed the Ctrl+V keys. Microsoft fixed it in mid-September. But it made a comeback in Excel 2016 when users installed October's security update . Microsoft has now released a new build of Excel 2016 to address the reintroduction of the bug: build 16.0.5574.1006. The company wrote: "The new build includes all security updates for Microsoft Excel 2016, and also fixes the issue that was reintroduced in 16.0.5574.1005, in which paste operations might fail if the workbook contains conditional formatting." Microsoft did not explain how the bug slipped back in. Copy and paste is, after all, a niche bit of functionality. Users reported the recurrence of the bug in October after the KB5002934 update was applied. Rolling back the update resolved the problem until Windows Update pushed the patch again. KB5002934 is a security update that resolves glitches including remote code execution and information disclosure vulnerabilities. The problem affects only Excel 2016 and is not the result of the latest Windows security update. Rather, it was reintroduced in an Excel update delivered through Windows Update. A user in a Microsoft Excel forum said the issue had appeared on workstations throughout their organization. "What's frustrating is that this is the same issue we encountered before, which was supposedly fixed in a previous update. Now it's back, barely a few weeks later." And now, at least, it appears to be fixed once again. Still, if Microsoft is determined to reintroduce bugs into Excel, perhaps it might also be tempted to bring back the Hall of Tortured Souls (a secret first-person 3D mini-game hidden inside Microsoft Excel for Windows 95) and populate it with the testers who managed to miss the issue's resurrection. ®

item.title: Tether and Tron Quietly Scrapped T3 Crime Unit Two Months Before $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Tether and Tron Quietly Scrapped T3 Crime Unit Two Months Before $6.3 Billion Binance Hack The T3 Financial Crime Unit, the anti-crime alliance Tron, Tether and TRM Labs launched in 2024 and later expanded to Binance, quietly shut down in late August, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, about two months before the record Binance hack. The alliance broke down over the past year amid slow response times and a lack of coordination among its members, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. One of them said T3 was terminated in late August. None of the companies announced the shutdown at the time. Tron, Tether and TRM confirmed that the initiative had wound down, without commenting on the details of the report. Binance declined to comment. “While the very successful T3 program has concluded, Tron remains committed to working to help stop illicit activities on the blockchain, in partnership with law enforcement,” a Tron DAO spokesperson said to Bloomberg . The spokesperson said Tron will share details of a new anti-crime initiative later. A Tether spokesperson said the company will keep working with TRM to disrupt illicit funds and has been taking part in Beacon Network, a real-time intelligence-sharing network TRM launched in August 2025. Tether is also working on the Financial Access and Systemic Empowerment Foundation, or FASE Foundation, which CEO Paolo Ardoino unveiled on X on Oct. 31. TRM’s global head of policy and government affairs, Ari Redbord, said “T3 achieved extraordinary things” and that “Beacon Network builds on that work.” What T3 was built to do Tron, Tether and TRM set up T3 in September 2024 as a public-private unit aimed at illicit use of Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the Tron blockchain. The pitch was speed. TRM supplied blockchain intelligence, Tron supplied network visibility and Tether supplied the power to freeze tokens at the issuer level. The unit said in August 2025 that it had frozen more than $250 million in illicit assets in less than a year. At the same time, it launched T3+, a program for outside partners, with Binance as its first member. Its first joint effort with the exchange froze almost $6 million tied to a pig-butchering scam. The totals kept climbing. TRM put the T3 tally above $300 million in February, when it announced a $70 million Series C round. In May, the unit announced that it had frozen more than $450 million and was working with authorities in 23 jurisdictions on five continents, including the U.S., Spain, Germany, Brazil and the U.K. That May release also said the unit had frozen funds within 24 hours of law enforcement requests in account takeovers and violent crime emergencies. It made no mention of the coordination problems Bloomberg has now described. TRM wrote that the Financial Action Task Force cited T3 in November 2025 guidance as a leading model for public-private enforcement work. item.title: Riot (RIOT) Names Anthropic as Tenant in $28 Billion Texas Lease, Could Owe It 12% Interest
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Riot (RIOT) Names Anthropic as Tenant in $28 Billion Texas Lease, Could Owe It 12% Interest Riot Platforms’ unnamed “Frontier AI Lab” is Anthropic, the bitcoin miner disclosed in its quarterly report filed Wednesday, naming the Claude developer as the tenant behind a 15-year lease worth about $28 billion on its Corsicana, Texas campus. The company’s results release on the same day described the tenant only as a “leading Frontier AI Lab.” The 10-Q is more specific. It says a Riot subsidiary signed the lease on Oct. 28 “with Anthropic PBC (the ‘Frontier AI Lab’),” and the deal became binding on Nov. 4 after Riot’s board approved it and outside consultants signed off on the technical specifications. The filing uses the same defined term for the tenant of Riot’s 191 MW Rockdale lease, signed in August. That makes Anthropic the counterparty on 1,101 MW of the 1,151 MW Riot has contracted. AMD holds the other 50 MW. The Corsicana lease covers 910 MW of critical IT capacity across the whole campus. Base rent starts at $130 per kilowatt per month and rises 3% a year. At that starting rate, the full 910 MW would bring in about $1.42 billion a year. Riot puts average annual rent at about $1.8 billion over the initial term, or roughly $54 billion in total if Anthropic exercises both five-year extensions. Riot’s 12% clause The detail drawing attention sits in the financing terms. The infrastructure company agreed to reimburse Anthropic up to $4 million per megawatt for the data center modules the tenant installs, or up to about $3.6 billion across the full 910 MW. That reimbursement depends on Riot raising money “on market terms reasonably acceptable to it.” If that financing is not available, the 10-Q says , Riot will instead give Anthropic rent credits that amortize the amount “plus interest at 12% per year” over the rest of the initial term. In that case, Anthropic would effectively finance the build itself and recover the cost out of rent at a double-digit rate. Riot’s base case is different. The company expects to fund the reimbursements with non-recourse project debt sized to the contracted rent, and it puts the total capital requirement at about $6 million per MW, or $5.5 billion. It said it does not currently expect to issue equity for the project. Deadlines and exits favor the tenant The lease puts most of the delivery risk on Riot. Capacity arrives in three phases: 400 MW with a first block targeted for June 28, 2027, 200 MW starting Dec. 24, 2027 and 310 MW on July 30, 2028. If Riot delivers more than 60 days late, Anthropic earns escalating rent credits capped at 270 days of base rent for the undelivered blocks. If a phase is not delivered within 270 days of its target, Anthropic can terminate the lease for that phase on 30 days’ notice, with extensions for force majeure of up to 365 days. Riot cannot curtail Anthropic’s power load or enroll the site in voluntary demand response programs without consent, a notable limit for a com

item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $79,600 as Oil Rebounds and Bank of England Hikes Rates
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $79,600 as Oil Rebounds and Bank of England Hikes Rates Bitcoin price traded near $79,600 on Thursday morning, up about 2% from a day earlier but roughly $21,900 below its price one year ago, after slipping back under $80,000 as oil prices recovered and the Bank of England raised interest rates, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. Bitcoin changed hands at $79,632 at 8:05 a.m. ET, with a market cap of about $1.60 trillion and roughly $35.2 billion in trading volume over the past day. The move gives back a slice of Wednesday’s rally. Bitcoin price held near $80,000 through Wednesday afternoon and stayed above that level overnight, peaking just under $80,900 around 5 p.m. ET. It dipped below $80,000 in the 7 a.m. ET hour on Thursday, as stock futures turned mixed and oil firmed. The pullback is small next to the week’s swing. Bitcoin sat near $75,600 on election night, so Thursday’s price is still more than 5% above that low. Oil and rates set the tone Oil drove Wednesday’s relief rally, and it is now taking some of that back. Brent crude futures rose $1.53, or 1.6%, to $96.15 a barrel on Thursday, while West Texas Intermediate added 52 cents to $88.64. Both benchmarks fell more than 8% on Wednesday to settle at their lowest since Aug. 31. “The situation in the Middle East is still unresolved and that’s why there is some modest recovery in prices at the moment,” UBS commodity analyst Giovanni Staunovo said . That matters for the bitcoin price because energy has been the main channel from the Iran war into inflation and interest rates. Cheaper crude eases pressure on the Federal Reserve. A rebound does the opposite. The Bank of England made that link explicit on Thursday. Its Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate by a quarter point to 4%, its first hike in more than three years, with the one dissenter, Catherine Mann, pushing for a half-point move. The bank said U.K. inflation is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year, citing energy prices tied to a conflict “now in its ninth month.” CNBC called it the last major central bank to start tightening since the war began, a reminder that global rates are still moving against risk assets. Stocks cool, ETFs return U.S. stock futures split Thursday morning after the Dow’s best session since April 2025. Dow futures rose 0.5% and S&P 500 futures added 0.1%, while Nasdaq-100 futures dropped about 0.5% as chip and data center stocks stayed under pressure. Fund demand picked up. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $74.6 million on Wednesday, ending a three-session run of outflows that totaled about $1.16 billion. Fidelity’s FBTC drew $236.7 million, more than offsetting a $201.2 million outflow from BlackRock’s IBIT. Supply from miners remains a weight. item.title: 2027: APC chairman seeks Ekiti voters’ support for Tinubu
item.description: National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has urged voters in Ekiti State to support President Bola Tinubu and other party candidates in the 2027 general elections, citing the administration’s economic reforms and development projects. Yilwatda made the appeal on Thursday at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where he joined Vice President Kashim Shettima, members of the party’s National Working Committee, governors and other stakeholders to present the party’s candidates to voters. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman expressed satisfaction with the turnout at the rally, describing it as a demonstration of support for the party and its Renewed Hope Agenda. He said the rally provided an opportunity to present the party’s candidates, including Tinubu and those seeking election into the National Assembly and Ekiti State House of Assembly. Yilwatda described Tinubu as a performer and reformer, saying his administration had introduced policies aimed at repositioning the economy, strengthening public institutions and creating opportunities for Nigerians. He particularly highlighted the administration’s tax reforms, arguing that the new framework was designed to protect low-income earners and small businesses from excessive tax burdens. The APC chairman also cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as an intervention to expand access to higher education, noting that eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly upkeep allowance of N20,000. On infrastructure, he highlighted federal road projects in Ekiti State, including major connections between Ado-Ekiti and Akure, as evidence of the administration’s commitment to improving transportation and economic activities. He urged voters to elect APC candidates across all elective positions, particularly in the National Assembly and state legislature, arguing that their presence would facilitate the implementation of the President’s development agenda. Yilwatda also called on party members and stakeholders in Ekiti to remain united and mobilised ahead of the elections. He expressed confidence that the APC would consolidate its political strength in 2027 and urged Nigerians to renew their support for Tinubu and the party. FCCPC seals firms as oil, salt samples fail fortification tests
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has sealed manufacturing facilities of defaulting food companies following a survey that revealed inadequate fortification of some vegetable oil and salt products sold in Nigerian markets. The commission also warned food manufacturers to comply with national micronutrient fortification standards, vowing to intensify enforcement against businesses that fail to meet statutory requirements. Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the FCCPC, Tunji Bello, disclosed this on Thursday while presenting the findings of a two-month market survey conducted in partnership with the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN). The survey examined 200 randomly selected samples, comprising 100 vegetable oil and 100 salt products collected from households and open markets across Northern and Southern Nigeria. Laboratory analysis showed that 12 per cent of the vegetable oil samples and two per cent of the salt samples were inadequately fortified with essential micronutrients at the household level. According to Bello, the survey covered both branded and unbranded products. Of the 100 vegetable oil samples, 49 were unbranded, while 51 were branded products, including Devon King’s, Power Oil, Activa, Golden Penny, Laziz, Mamador and Golden Terra, among others. Similarly, 19 of the 100 salt samples were unbranded, while 81 were branded products, comprising 71 samples of Mr Chef and 10 of Dangote salt. The investigation also identified significant gaps in the adoption of digital traceability systems designed to monitor the quality of fortified food products from manufacturing facilities to retail outlets. Bello said the survey used GAIN’s Digital Fortification Quality Traceability Plus (DFQT+) platform to track compliance and promote transparency across the food supply chain. However, regulatory data showed that only six vegetable oil manufacturers had registered on the platform, while just three companies uploaded a combined eight product test results out of the 100 oil samples analysed. He stressed that large-scale food fortification was a mandatory public health policy designed to address micronutrient deficiencies by requiring food processors to enrich staple products with essential nutrients, including vitamin A, iron, folic acid, zinc and iodine. He said the policy was particularly important in tackling hidden hunger and nutritional deficiencies among young children and women of reproductive age. “Consumers must be able to trust the quality of the products they buy and the health benefits those products are advertised to provide. “Consumer protection goes beyond resolving everyday complaints or halting deceptive business practices. It fundamentally comes down to ensuring that citizens are not denied the essential value, safety and nutritional benefits they pay for in the marketplace,” Bello said. item.title: NASA announces experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft: A 'new beginning for aeronautics'
item.description: null NASA has revealed a glimpse of its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal. Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane , or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement . The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke. Little can be gleaned from the image about what final form the X-70 might take, but the tail fins are somewhat reminiscent of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor or Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet . "The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the statement. The NASA chief called the aircraft "just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics" and said that the agency expects the X-70 to make its first flight within two years. "This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly," Isaacman added. NASA's statement fleshes out a few details about the X-70's capabilities. According to the agency, Fractal will fly at a cruise speed of Mach .75, about the same as a Boeing 737 Classic. The X-70 will be able to reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet (13.7 kilometers), and will have a range exceeding 1,726 miles (2,777 kilometers, or 1,500 nautical miles). The X-70 Fractal will also be able to carry around 2,000 pounds (900 kg) of experimental payloads both internally and externally, which will allow for a "wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities," NASA said in the statement. NASA adds it will have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,535 kilograms), around the same weight as the Scaled Composites- and Northrop Grumman-developed Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft. In fact, the two aircraft share a similar silhouette — at least in the AI image of the X-70 Fractal NASA has released so far. Scaled Composites' Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft (top); NASA's render of its upcoming X-70 Fractal (bottom). (Image credit: Northrop Grumman/NASA) The agency's most recent X-plane, the X-59 , has been flying for over a year. That jet features a radical long-nosed geometry without a forward windscreen; pilots fly by way of an augmented reality screen that combines views from sensors and a forward-facing camera. That geometry dampens the shockwaves coming off of the X-59 when it flies faster than the sound barrier, allowing it to fly at speeds over Mach 1 without the thunderous sonic booms that typically accompany supersonic flight. item.title: 'Stop dirty datacenters': Europe-wide protests planned demanding building moratorium
item.description: Campaigners against datacenter expansion are planning two days of coordinated action across Europe on November 6 and 7, demanding an immediate moratorium on new large-scale developments. Following the US midterm elections , where restrictions on massive AI server farms were prominent in the campaigns from candidates in both major parties, it's now Europe's turn. Over 100 groups across 15 European countries will protest the boom in bit barn building over the next couple of days. As well as demonstrations, there will be public meetings, stalls, petitions, walking tours, cycle rides, poetry readings and other creative actions, the organizers say. The coalition of groups has put up a website – stopdirtydatacentres.eu – with an interactive map allowing anyone to find information on the events taking place and where. In the UK, there is a photocall planned at 8am on November 6 outside the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) in Whitehall Place in central London, but also a Community Day of Action the following day at London's Brick Lane, where a facility is planned on the site of the former Truman Brewery. Also on November 7, there will be a "family event" at St Michaels & All Angels Church in Great Torrington, Devon, to highlight the massive 1.5 GW data campus and on-site battery energy storage that is planned for 850 acres of farmland near the town. The planned actions are a response to growing concerns about the impact of the wave of new compute shed projects on local communities, public infrastructure, land, water and energy use, housing, jobs and the cost of living. Such concerns won't have been helped by recent events, such as a Google subsidiary reportedly felling 250,000 trees illegally in Finland to clear the ground for a server hall. The campaigners claim that governments, the European Union and the tech giants are gambling with the future by racing ahead with server farm developments without proper scrutiny of the environmental, democratic and social impacts they might have. A recent report found that businesses and private-sector trade associations dominated meetings with UK ministers to discuss datacenters, while environmental groups didn't get a look-in. Campaigners are calling for an immediate moratorium on new large-scale projects across Europe, until clear frameworks are in place to determine whether new facilities should be built and under what conditions, with proper scrutiny and meaningful public participation. "Datacenter developers in the UK and Europe want to cash in on the AI goldrush whatever the consequences. But communities everywhere are fighting back, seeing through Big Tech's PR machine and calling this what it is – a massive grab of scarce land, water and power resources by Silicon Valley billionaires," said Oliver Hayes, Head of Campaigns at Global Action Plan (UK). item.title: NSCDC Smashes Border Gang Hideout In Ebonyi
item.description: Operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Ebonyi State Command, have dismantled a criminal syndicate operating along the Ebonyi-Benue border, recovering an AK-47 rifle, live ammunition, and various dangerous items during a targeted sting operation. The operation, which targeted hideouts used by hoodlums and cult groups operating between Izzi Local Government Area in Ebonyi and neighboring Benue State, followed a week-long intelligence-gathering exercise. The raid was jointly executed by operatives from the Command’s Intelligence and Investigation Department alongside the State Commandant’s Special Squad. Briefing newsmen on Thursday at the Command Headquarters in Abakaliki, the State Commandant, Francis Nnadi, confirmed the success of the multi-location operation, highlighting the professional conduct of the officers during the raid on the fleeing suspects and their collaborators. During the sweep of the enclave, security operatives recovered the following items: 1 AK-47 rifle, 1 double-loaded magazine, 4 rounds of live ammunition, 1 locally-made pistol, 1 pump-action gun, 5 tactical knives, and assorted criminal charms. Issuing a strong warning to criminal networks operating within the state, Commandant Nnadi emphasized that the Command, in close synergy with sister security agencies, remains steadfast in wiping out criminality across Ebonyi. “I want to warn criminal elements ahead of the general elections to flee Ebonyi State. The Command, in conjunction with other sister security agencies, is fully prepared to rid the state of all forms of crime and criminality,” Nnadi stated. He further reassured residents in border areas and across the state of robust security coverage throughout the electoral season. “I want to assure residents of the border communities and the entire state of adequate security before, during, and after the elections.” “I urge the public to continue providing credible, timely information to assist security agencies in maintaining law and order,” he added. Manhunt operations are currently underway to track down and apprehend the fleeing suspects. The post NSCDC Smashes Border Gang Hideout In Ebonyi appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ADC Rejects Judgment Voiding Atiku’s Candidacy, Accuses APC Of Desperation To Cripple Opposition
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has rejected the judgment by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which sacked the Senator David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated the candidacy of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. The party described the judgment as another desperate attempt by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. It added that the November 4 presidential campaign rally in Sokoto State sent the APC into panic. In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, on Thursday, the party said the timing of the judgment, barely 24 hours after the massive turnout at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Sokoto, exposed what it considers the growing desperation of the APC. “We have reasons to believe that the judgment had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery,” it stated. “Yesterday, Nigerians came out in their hundreds of thousands to demonstrate their support for the ADC and our promise of making life affordable for them. Today, they are being told that the party that they support and the candidates that they have supported at all levels could be erased by the stroke of a reckless judicial pen.” The opposition party questioned “whether those behind the flawed judgment” had considered its far-reaching implications for the country. It warned that the attempt to invalidate the party’s leadership could affect thousands of candidates contesting elections at the local, state and federal levels. “Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process,” it added. The ADC maintained that the judgment was legally indefensible and would be challenged through every available judicial process. “Our objection is particularly anchored on the subsisting judgment of Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, delivered on 2 July 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025, which affirmed the legitimacy of the David Mark-led NWC and directed INEC to recognise the leadership. It is a settled principle of Nigerian jurisprudence that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot sit on appeal over, review, vary or nullify the subsisting judgment of another court of equal jurisdiction,” it said. “The ADC, therefore, rejects any consequential orders founded on a determination that appears to disregard these fundamental legal principles. However, we await the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the said judgment to ascertain its precise terms, scope and operative orders.” Atiku (centre) is the presidential candidate of the ADC for the 2027 general elections. item.title: Motorola's new Signature 27 has it all if you can stomach the $1,600 price tag
item.description: Motorola is patching a hole in its US lineup with a non-folding flagship phone, but the pricing puts this device dangerously close to the company's expensive tablet-style foldable . The long-rumored Motorola Signature 27 is real, featuring top-of-the-line specs, a super-bright OLED screen, and a ton of cameras. But all this high-end hardware won't come cheap in the age of AI. Motorola's new flagship smartphone will run a whopping $1,600 when it arrives later this month. The Signature 27 is a completely new take on flagship smartphones from Motorola, leaving behind the middling legacy of the Edge series. However, you'll still immediately clock this as a Motorola device due to its distinctive use of materials and Pantone colors. The phone is metal, ceramic, and glass, but the backs are textured polycarbonate. The device comes in Coal Smoke (black) or Capulet Olive (green) colors. The former has a "tactical weave" finish inspired by automotive design, and the latter is "textile-inspired." This device will include the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, the most powerful mobile chip Qualcomm offers right now. While some smartphones have flirted with 16GB of memory, that's less common these days. The Signature 27 will have 12GB like Samsung's base model flagships. However, there's not going to be an upgrade option for more. You will, however, get a generous 512GB of storage. Read full article Comments

item.title: China lays out plans to land astronauts on the moon 'before 2030.' Can NASA still win this race?
item.description: null China has given us some details about the epic moon landing it plans to pull off a few years from now. Chinese officials laid out the roadmap for its crewed lunar campaign at the 7th Manned Space Symposium, which was held Oct. 31 and Nov. 1 in Beijing. The campaign consists of four missions, culminating in a crewed touchdown "before 2030," according to media reports . That timeline — which is consistent with previous statements made by the China Manned Space Agency — keeps the pressure on the U.S., which aims to put its own astronauts down on the moon in 2028, via NASA's Artemis program . Leaked slide confirms the four-mission progression toward China’s crewed lunar landing:🚀2027: Maiden flight of Long March 10A carrying Mengzhou CSS cargo resupply mission, to validate the new human-rated vehicle and Mengzhou’s orbital operations in LEO.🚀2028: First flight of the heavier CZ-10 with an uncrewed Lanyue lander performing a lunar descent and ascent test, exercising the lander’s propulsion and guidance.🚀🚀2029: Dual CZ-10 launches of Mengzhou and Lanyue for a full-scale lunar-orbit rehearsal, demonstrating rendezvous, docking, and integrated operations.🚀🚀Before the end of 2030: Dual CZ-10 crewed lunar landing mission. November 1, 2026 China shooting for the moon The first mission in China's four-part lunar campaign is scheduled to fly in 2027, according to CNSpaceflight , an X account that keeps a close eye on China's activities in space. The outlet cited an X user who shared a presentation slide of the plan. That launch — the first of of China's new Long March 10A rocket — will send an uncrewed Mengzhou spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO) for a series of tests. Mengzhou , whose name means "Dream Vessel," is the next-gen crew capsule that will carry Chinese astronauts to lunar orbit. Mission number two, launching in 2028, will involve a different set of hardware — the more powerful Long March 10 rocket and the Lanyue ("Embracing the Moon") lunar lander. This will also be an uncrewed flight, and it will mark the debut of the Long March 10, which will send Lanyue to orbit around the moon. If all goes to plan, Lanyue will touch down on the moon and then launch itself back to lunar orbit. Mission number three, flying in 2029, will also target an uncrewed lunar landing, but it will feature two Long March 10 launches — one apiece for Mengzhou and Lanyue. The two spacecraft will conduct a rendezvous and docking rehearsal in lunar orbit, then separate for Lanyue's trip down to the surface. This will set the stage for mission four — the real deal, in which two Long March 10s launch a crewed Mengzhou and an uncrewed Lanyue "before 2030." The two vessels will dock in lunar orbit, and the astronauts will move into Lanyue for their historic lunar landing. Three astronauts will apparently launch on Mengzhou, and two of them will land on the moon aboard Lanyue, according to CNSpaceflight . The duo will spend three days on the lunar surface, conducting moonwalks

item.title: Anthropic won't fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
item.description: A vulnerability in Anthropic’s Claude products lets any browser extension that can control Claude Dispatch make Claude Desktop run code on the computer – or even a different machine signed into the same Claude account – with no browser exploit and minimal user interaction required. Anthropic, aware of the problem since May, has taken no action to close the hole. Dispatch is a feature in Claude that lets users send and manage tasks from their mobile phone or browser to Claude Desktop, an AI agent that runs commands on their computer. Forever Security researcher Gal Weizman discovered that Claude Dispatch’s interface and API were reachable from an ordinary logged-in web session at claude.ai. So a browser extension able to control claude.ai could send commands to Claude Desktop as if they came from the legitimate Dispatch user. “That extension was able to perform a classic escalation of privileges. Because now Claude has access to the files in the operating system, it can run code on the operating system and compromise the machine completely,” said Weizman. “We’re talking about millions of installs.” Claude.ai received about 950 million monthly visits as of mid-2026, and Cowork usage included 1.2 million sampled sessions from more than 600,000 organizations during May, according to Anthropic’s usage data. Weizman found and disclosed the Claude Dispatch flaw, dubbed ThisBash, to Anthropic, and shared his research exclusively with The Register . The AI company acknowledged his report as a valid vulnerability in May, but closed the security issue as a duplicate of a known flaw it was already tracking. Anthropic did not pay Weizman a bug bounty or issue a CVE, but told him it planned to retire Dispatch at the end of October. That didn’t happen. The Claudefather did not respond to The Register ’s questions – including when it planned to retire the feature – but as of October 30, the official Claude support page listed Dispatch as available in limited beta on some Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, but not available to new users. “If you already use Dispatch, you can keep using it for now,” the page reads . Even if Anthropic does kill off Dispatch, Weizman says the fundamental flaw in Claude’s design still exists, and the security weakness now lives on in other features like Claude Code Remote Control and Claude Cowork sessions. The researcher told us he communicated all of this to Anthropic. “They still decided not to do anything about it,” Weizman said. “Claude Cowork is now accessible via the web version, and it shares the same sessions as you can access in the desktop version,” he said. “Once again, using an extension, you can use the Cowork sessions to say: ‘Please access this file and grab it. Please install this malicious npm package. Please run code on the operating system.’ And it would.” Weizman said his research “started with a vulnerability. And it ended up being a design choice that enables this attack vector very easily.” There is a prerequisite for

item.description: Explore Hubble Hubble Home Overview About Hubble The History of Hubble Hubble Timeline Why Have a Telescope in Space? Hubble by the Numbers At the Museum FAQs Impact & Benefits Hubble’s Impact & Benefits Science Impacts Cultural Impact Technology Benefits Impact on Human Spaceflight Astro Community Impacts Science Hubble Science Science Themes Science Highlights Science Behind Discoveries Universe Uncovered Hubble’s Partners in Science Hubble & Citizen Science SI & Hubble Science Explore the Night Sky Observatory Hubble Observatory Hubble Design Mission Operations Science Operations Astronaut Missions to Hubble Hubble vs. Webb Hubble vs. Roman Team Hubble Team Career Aspirations Hubble Astronauts Multimedia Images Videos Online Activities e-Books Sonifications Podcasts 3D Hubble Models Lithographs Fact Sheets Posters Hubble on the NASA App Glossary News Hubble News Social Media Media Resources 35th Anniversary More Online Activities 3 min read Hubble Learns Galactic History From Stars This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image features the globular star cluster called Messier 30 (M30), also called NGC 7099. ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image provides a lesson in galactic history. The sparkling collection of stars is named Messier 30 (M30) after the French astronomer, Charles Messier , who cataloged M30 and other diffuse objects that might be mistaken for comets in the early telescopes of Messier’s time. M30 lies about 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster : a roughly spherical grouping of stars containing anywhere from tens of thousands to millions of stars. These clusters generally reside on the outskirts of galaxies, orbiting within a vast, diffuse region called the halo like a swarm of moths around a lightbulb. Our Milky Way galaxy has at least 150 globular clusters, the nearest of which is about 6,000 light-years away. These clusters are impressively ancient: astronomers estimate their ages are between 11.5 to 13.5 billion years, making certain globular clusters nearly as old as the universe itself. Globular clusters have long played an important role in helping us learn about our galaxy. More than a century ago, astronomer Harlow Shapley used observations of a particular type of variable star to measure the locations of and distances to dozens of globular clusters within our galaxy. His work showed that the Sun is not in the center of our galaxy, and that the galactic center lies toward the constellation Sagittarius. (His distance measurements were incorrect, however, and he concluded that our galaxy is about twice as large as it really is.) Today, astronomers continue to learn about our galaxy by observing globular clusters. Because globular clusters are so ancient, they can give us clues about how our galaxy developed long ago. item.title: New York's Queens Public Library battles ransomware crims: Wi-Fi, checkouts, and website go dark
item.description: New York City's Queens Public Library (QPL) is battling a ransomware attack, it confirmed on Wednesday evening via social media and to patrons directly. The disruption has downed QPL's website, on-site computers, check-out and return machines, its public Wi-Fi, mobile app, and its digital media services. Renewals are also unavailable, although library users are not charged fines for returning materials late. (Since 2021, In October 2021, QPL, Brooklyn Public Library, and New York Public Library - in an effort to help lower income users from being put off borrowing - permanently killed daily late fines on books and circulating materials .) Each of the library system's 66 locations remains open, including the central library in the Jamaica neighborhood in Queens, but QPL warned: "it will take some time before the library's network and systems are restored." QPL said "certain virtual and in-person programs may be impacted," advising visitors to check availability with their local branch via phone, and check the library's social media channels for official updates. "Our IT department is working to resolve the issue, and we will keep you informed,” it said in the statement. It added: "We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your patience." No established ransomware group has yet claimed responsibility for the disruption, although attacks on publicly funded institutions rarely lead to lucrative payouts. The British Library's infamous ransomware attack in 2023 at the hands of Rhysida saw the organization refuse to pay the criminals' 20 Bitcoin ransom demand, opting instead to drain its cash reserves and fork out millions for an IT rebuild . Although the library's response to the attack drew widespread praise, few institutions of its kind are in a financial position to follow its lead. Other libraries might not be willing or able to commit to a recovery period as lengthy as that of the British Library . In its 2025/26 annual report , published in July, the institution said its recovery is still incomplete, and work to fully restore customers' ability to purchase electronic resources, such as journals and research databases, and reopen access to electronic legal deposit content is ongoing. This is likely to be completed by the end of 2026, the British Library added. ®

item.title: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market
item.description: Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States. The robotics company, headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously became the first to achieve full-time commercial deployment of humanoid robots at a customer warehouse in 2024. Now, Agility’s public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange as of November 5 has come with financial disclosures detailing how the company plans to build a business around renting out or selling humanoid robots to perform manual labor. “When we are doing robots as a service, it is much lower risk for customers to use it because they are getting a return on investment on day one,” Jonathan Hurst , co-founder and chief robot officer at Agility Robotics, told Ars. "Because they're paying a rate that is comparable to the human labor rate, and that makes the economics pretty straightforward.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Norway's aid agency pwned and all users' data is stolen
item.description: Norway's national aid agency, Norad, has confirmed that cyber criminals broke into its systems, stealing information about each and every registered user of its grant portal. Norad, which coordinates Norway's assistance for foreign development, said that 20,614 registered individuals had their names and email addresses swiped, and information from at least three organizations' applications was "misdirected." The agency clarified that the grant portal, which was launched in 2017, has 20,614 registered users, meaning all were affected, across 12,511 organizations. In addition, the grant applications for at least three organizations are confirmed to be involved, though Norad said it may discover more as its investigation continues. Torger Kjeldstad, director of digitalization at Norad, said "the attack is complex," and confirmed the agency has initiated a crisis team to manage it. "We know a lot about what has happened, but to ensure that we have a complete overview of the attack, we are working to engage external experts in cybersecurity," he said. "They will give us a detailed description of what information those who attacked the solution have gained access to." Kjeldstad added that "it should be safe" to continue using Norad's services while it continues to probe what happened, and who was behind it. Norad did not reveal many details about how the attack unfolded, other than saying that 27 accounts were compromised and were then used to gain access to the portal and the data in question. The agency said the intrusion was detected on October 30, but did not offer any indication as to how long the attackers retained access to the grant portal. It also refused to rule out that names of applicants in "conflict areas and authoritarian states" may have been included in the stolen data – it is not known if recipients would have also been registered users – and said it is approaching the matter "very seriously." The grant portal, managed by Norad, which itself is part of Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is responsible for handling applications from organizations across the world. Recent case studies include support for independent, investigative journalism in Moldova, a country which routinely battles Russian propaganda and election interference, and backing for Ukrainian children and prisoners of war. The issues Norad and the Norwegian government support, however, are wide-ranging – from access to healthcare for transgender people worldwide and Kenyan incubators for innovative transport solutions, to delivering aid to war-torn Gaza. ®

Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . In attendance was also award-winning American-born actress and producer Osas Ighodaro . Guests also experienced a new fashion themed game developed by Lagos based Maliyo Games, highlighting fashion’s growing links with technology and entertainment. Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele speaking at the event hosted by the U.S. Consul General in her honor, celebrating her vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. Fashion is a major global industry, supporting jobs and commercial activity across design, retail, and related sectors including in both the United States and Nigeria. U.S. consumers spent an estimated $560 billion on clothing and footwear in 2025, according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. For Nigeria’s fashion industry, access to the American market offers a pathway to expand the reach of Nigerian designers while offering entry points into Africa for U.S. retailers and businesses. Since founding Lagos Fashion Week in 2011, Omoyemi Akerele has built the platform into one of Africa’s leading fashion showcases. Its 2025 edition featured more than 60 designers and welcomed approximately 15,000 guests. Lagos Fashion Week (LFW) has also become a bridge to the American fashion industry. Leading American singer Ciara walked the LFW runway in 2025, while Studio 189, the label co-founded by American actress Rosario Dawson , has shown collections in Lagos. New York-based Nigerian designer Tia Adeola has also featured her collections at LFW as well as American media outlets including Vogue and Essence being among the leading U.S. outlets that have covered the shows. LFW helps Nigerian designers explore the U.S. market through trade shows such as Coterie and NYNOW in New York and Liberty Fairs in Miami. item.title: SAP promises to open out data flows in both directions
item.description: SAP has taken meaningful steps in opening its data to bidrectional sharing across the enterprise, and in decoupling the advanced analytics needed for AI from its ERP upgrade path. During a technical conference last week, the German software giant adopted native support for Apache Iceberg, the open table format, and extended its partnership with Databricks to bring data from legacy ERP systems into its modern cloud analytics platform. "By putting [a] stake in the ground with Iceberg, we now have SAP moving from a very closed application storage model to an open lakehouse model," said Aaron Rosenbaum, Gartner senior director analyst, referring to the concept which brings together data lakes and warehouses. Also important was the bridge between modern analytics in the cloud and on-prem or hosted legacy systems such as ECC, the ERP system broadly adopted by global companies. "SAP made a pretty big move in saying we're going to open this up, not just to S/4HANA Cloud [the latest ERP system], but ECC users. That coupling — leveraging of AI, leveraging a lakehouse for AI to the ERP upgrade lifecycle — was a problem," said Rosenbaum. In May this year, SAP bought Dremio, a lakehouse platform built around Apache Iceberg, ending its previous preference for Databricks' Delta Sharing to bring together SAP data products with existing lakehouses bi-directionally. At SAP's TedEd conference last week, SAP said its Business Data Cloud (BDC) – the "trusted data foundation for SAP Business AI Platform" – would now support native Apache Iceberg and a universal catalog powered by Apache Polaris, "providing an open and governed data foundation for users and [AI agent platform] Joule to consume data." Together with SAP BDC Connect, the new tech policy will support platform interoperability with "zero-copy data sharing" across platforms from Databricks, Snowflake, Google, AWS, and Microsoft. The system would also continue to support Delta Lake, the alternative open table format from Databricks, SAP said . With the integration of Dremio's SQL query engine, BDC users will also get access to relational databases including SQL Server, MongoDB, Oracle, and PostgreSQL without moving data, the vendor said. During the same conference, Databricks – the lakehouse company born out of an Apache Spark platform – extended its partnership with SAP based on the previously announced SAP Databricks, which embeds the Databricks Data + AI Platform in BDC. That "expanded scope" promises to make data from SAP applications available for consumption in the SAP Business Data Cloud engine of choice, including SAP Databricks. The vendor said that a manufacturer running finance and supply chain on SAP ECC on-premises, for example, could use SAP Application Data Foundation to bring historic order data into SAP Databricks, combining it with third-party data, and allowing data engineers to build demand-forecasting models on SAP's business semantics, without custom extraction pipelines. item.title: Royal London plans IT outsourcing shake-up as staff brace for redundancies
item.description: Royal London plans to cut hundreds of IT jobs and shift work to India under an outsourcing deal with IBM, according to sources, with redundancies expected by the end of December. Sources said Royal London's chief technology officer, James Sandell, told IT staff in September that the insurance and pensions giant was partnering with IBM to outsource a substantial portion of its technology operations. A consultation process was expected to follow. A Royal London spokesperson told The Register : "Royal London has appointed IBM as its strategic technology infrastructure partner as it continues to develop its technology strategy. The partnership will give Royal London access to IBM’s specialist capability, scale and experience. Royal London will remain accountable for service delivery and regulatory requirements and continues to focus on ensuring continuity and quality of service for customers." We asked Royal London how many UK IT roles it would retain and whether IBM would move work to India. The exact number of jobs at risk remains unclear, although one Glassdoor review posted on October 6 claims that hundreds of positions in the company's technology operations division are being eliminated. "A vast amount of knowledge is being lost by the business, a lot that is not yet documented due to constant years of recruitment freeze and workload volume," they wrote. The reviewer also questioned whether management had grasped just how much work would be involved in handing operations over to IBM, particularly with already stretched teams being cut to a fraction of their former size. Royal London replied to the Glassdoor review, acknowledging staff concerns about the changes, though it didn't comment on the claims about outsourcing and redundancies. "We recognise that as Royal London is going through a period of transformation, this has raised questions and concerns for some colleagues," the company wrote. "We have established channels for colleagues to raise these, including through People Leaders and Colleague Representatives, and I encourage colleagues to use these routes to discuss their concerns." Other October reviews questioned the handling of the outsourcing and Royal London's commitment to its mutual values. An October 12 reviewer identifying themselves as an IT infrastructure employee said the company had historically offered good career prospects, before criticizing its new direction. "Sudden outsourcing goes against all Royal London values," the reviewer wrote, adding that employees were questioning the company's direction amid reports of a hiring freeze and further potential cuts. Another review, posted on October 20, suggested the IBM deal was the latest in a series of outsourcing decisions following an earlier move to transfer servicing jobs to South Africa. "A mutual company but not mutual values when it comes to things like this," the reviewer claimed. The planned cuts follow rising profits. Royal London reported adjusted group operating prof

item.title: Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe first drive: Where tech and fun collide
item.description: Mercedes-Benz provided flights from San Francisco to Malaga, Spain, and accommodation so Ars could drive the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. The night before I drove the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, I complained to a group of journalists that automakers don't want to take chances and just build fun, weird cars anymore. About 12 hours later, Mercedes made me eat my words. Outside of all the bombastic extravaganza of the Los Angeles launch, the first true AMG powered exclusively by batteries is a technological triumph that's as comfortable on the track as it is on the street. And it's really very good on the track. Triforce One of the fundamental problems with EVs is weight. Batteries are heavy, and the old rule about an object in motion tending to stay in motion makes the notion of nimble cornering a difficult engineering problem. Mercedes loves an engineering problem, and after two days behind the wheel of the AMG GT EV, the company has mostly reduced the battery-weight tax that mires EV performance. On the road and on the track, the vehicle is firmly planted to the roadway. Mercedes says various technologies make this possible. In addition to decades of producing high-performance vehicles, the automaker's AMG.EA sports-car architecture does a lot of heavy lifting here, constantly adjusting power delivery from the three motors while guiding the Active Ride Control suspension, steering—including up to 6 degrees at the rear axle—and active aerodynamics to deliver the performance AMG customers have come to expect from a vehicle with the Affalterbach badge on the hood. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2 astronauts will finish upgrading ISS solar arrays during spacewalk today: Watch it live
item.description: null Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live. NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency 's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com , courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon points his camera toward his spacesuit’s helmet visor and takes a selfie during a spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Today's extravehicular activity (EVA) will be the second in a week for Menon and Kutryk, who installed the station's seventh iROSA during an Oct. 29 spacewalk . That excursion was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the ISS to date, and the first EVA for a Canadian astronaut since 2019. Today's spacewalk will wrap up an ambitious ISS power upgrade that has taken more than five years to pull off. "The installation job will complete the years-long process that began in June 2021 to augment the space station’s power generating capacity from 160 kilowatts to about 215 kilowatts," NASA officials wrote about the EVA in a blog post on Tuesday (Nov. 3) . That's a boost of about 30%. Menon and Kutryk are currently sharing the ISS with five other astronauts — NASA's Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov. Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov and Watkins arrived at the ISS on Oct. 1, on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission . Dubrov, Kikina and Menon got there in mid-July, aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

item.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
item.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. item.title: When datacenters lose power, generators should kick in. That didn’t happen for Google in London
item.description: Google Cloud has revealed that the cause of the October 20 outage in its europe-west-2-b availability zone was a ‘misconfiguration’ of its systems that meant its emergency generators didn’t start. The outage at the London facility caused service interruptions at outfits including Lloyds, HSBC, Royal Mail, and Revolut . In a November 4 update to its service status page, Google explained what went wrong. “The site relies on a 2N utility power architecture — where the facility has complete duplicate power paths for every critical load — backed by a central high-voltage generator bank managed by a dual-redundant Programmable Logic Controller (PLC),” Google revealed. The facility gets its juice from two independent utility feeders, which Google calls “A” and “B”. There’s also a “standby utility connection configured for manual campus-wide transfer during maintenance operations or emergency events.” Google says the root cause of the incident was failure in an external underground cable through which its power supplier brings ‘leccy to its bit barns. That cable connects to primary feeder A and it broke at a time when feeder B wasn’t working. “Circuit breaker feeder B was physically opened to allow for corrective repairs following issues identified during a quarterly generator load test on 14 Oct 2026,” Google admitted. “Consequently, primary utility feed A was supporting the total critical load while the feed B breaker remained in an open position to allow repairs to be conducted on the B feeder pathway.” That shouldn’t be a problem for a top-tier operator like Google, which knows it needs to install backup sources of electricity like uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) and on-site generators. Indeed, europe-west-2-b employs UPSes that Google says can keep things up and running for five minutes if the availability zone loses its connection to the grid. The UPSes worked, but a “voltage-sensing design flaw and PLC misconfiguration prevented the facility’s generator plant from receiving an automatic start signal to assume the critical load.” Google’s UPSes therefore ran out of juice, but its generators didn’t start. The rest is history. The search giant has figured out that its PLCs weren’t set up to handle the conditions it faced on this fateful day. “PLC logic indicated that a healthy utility source was available, even though the primary and secondary distribution feeds were de-energized, and did not issue a start command to the generator plant,” the status update reveals. Once Google was able to reconnect to its power utility, it reprogrammed the PLC so it wouldn’t make the same mistake again. The Big G has since made many changes to the electrical setup at europe-west-2-b and says it’s tested them and that they all work. It’s also given itself two action items, one of which it describes as a “Communications Enhancement” that will see it “bolster notification speed by developing an automated alert-to-communication mechanism for location-impacting incid
